formal_entries.label: qu:i-good-no-bmp
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:i-good-no-bmp}
Extend the complete topology of \cref{thm:positive-model-complete-metric} to ordinary models of zero lower volume and beyond bounded mass, retaining analytic closure exactly at the ideal models. Recover the curve topology of \cref{cor:curve-model-completeness} and the background compatibility of \cref{sec:model-background-comparison,sec:two-sided-model-backgrounds}, including higher-dimensional limits that lose bigness or positive lower volume.
formal_entries.state: The full curve-map model theorem now permits critical fibers; fixed-weight ideal extension is distinct from the all-weight type correspondence. The full curve model theorem now allows every smooth base form of nonnegative area, including the zero-area singleton. A stated finite factor of degree d gives two normalizations whose ratio is d; pushforward to the original base can lose component data. Classical curve-target factorization is now proved internally, so the finite-factor metric applies to every compact surjective curve map. General higher-rank backgrounds and cross-background complete topology remain open. Finite curve pullback now commutes with ordinary and ideal envelopes below pulled-back obstacles. Polar metric and volume scale by degree; the original-base model subspace is closed and complete with a mass-preserving 1-Lipschitz averaging retraction that commutes with ideal projection. The cubic analytic example shows that this retraction need not be nearest. General higher-rank and cross-background topology remains open.

formal_entries.label: qu:nef-degeneration-exponent
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:nef-degeneration-exponent}
Which geometric conditions on a nonclosed nef background force a common degeneration order, or an integral one? When is equality attained in the modification and residual order comparisons?
formal_entries.state: Both orders lie in $[0,n]$ and are independent of $\mu$ and $h$, of positive scaling, and of smooth gauge. For closed nef backgrounds on a K\"ahler manifold they equal $n-\operatorname{nd}(\theta)$. Nonclosed examples on products of elliptic curves realize unequal orders, irrational common orders, and zero volume with decay slower than every positive power. A modification can strictly increase the orders; effective residual subtraction also gives a one-sided comparison. Explicit elliptic threefolds have integral orders determined by the rank of their boundary forms. The flat-torus criterion separates current rigidity from rank: a nonzero semipositive boundary class is rigid exactly when its kernel leaves are dense, equivalently when a fixed positive perturbation collapses in diameter (Book, Theorem~28.16.1, printed p.~1410). Irrational and rational kernel slopes give the two alternatives (Book, Example~28.16.1, printed p.~1411). Arbitrary approaching flat K\"ahler forms can collapse at a nonrigid limiting class (Book, Example~28.16.2, printed p.~1412). These metric distinctions do not supply the nonclosed degeneration-order conditions asked for here. A Kummer resolution also has a nonzero smooth semipositive, nonrigid irrational boundary class with square zero (Book, Proposition~28.17.1, printed p.~1414). A global periodic $\ddc$ primitive identifies the representatives' Bott--Chern classes, and two explicitly translated torus periods detect the irrational ray. The resolved surface contains sixteen exceptional curves (Book, Lemma~28.17.1, printed p.~1413); the example does not address the curve-free regime of P11.\par Book, Lemma~26.19.3, printed p.~1175 proves a full-Gauduchon-infimum comparison when $\theta\leq CB$ and $\theta+\ddc\varphi\geq cB$, with $\varphi\in L^1$, $c,C>0$, and $B$ closed semipositive on a compact K\"ahler manifold. Constant rank $R$ gives two-sided variational-volume bounds by $\epsilon^{n-R}$ for arbitrary smooth positive probability and Hermitian perturbation. Theorem~26.19.1, printed p.~1177 constructs such a comparison for products of projective spaces and their linear-center blowups. The fixed cone has nonnegative parameters in $\theta=\sum_i((a_i+b_if_i)H_i+(c_i+d_ig_i)Q_i)$, with strictly positive fixed smooth $f_i,g_i$, omitted $Q_i$ terms on plain factors, and fixed pullback Fubini--Study generators. These functions may depend on every product coordinate. Each $H_i$-active block contributes $m_i$ to $R$, each $Q_i$-only blown block contributes $m_i-\ell_i-1$, and an inactive block contributes zero. All zero parameters and the zero background are included. An exceptional-divisor logarithm supplies the lower current bound; no restricted invariant/product test or Monge--Amp\`ere mass extremum replaces the variational infimum.\par Proposition~26.19.10, printed p.~1178 preserves this order under every specified product linear blowup and, more generally, every modification with compact K\"ahler manifold source. In the latter case the book also proves two-sided power bounds, using the closed-background intersection polynomial after pulling back the actual nonzero divisor sections. The upstairs probability is independently smooth and positive; a degenerate pullback probability is not used in the smooth dual formula.\par Lemma~26.19.4, printed p.~1179 determines the exact numerical range of the specified finite effective real sums of zero divisors of sections of integer tensor powers of the $H_i,Q_i$ bundles, with their fixed metrics: $\delta_i\geq0$ on plain factors and $\delta_i\geq0$, $\delta_i+\rho_i\geq0$ on blown factors. Theorem~26.19.2, printed p.~1180 assumes the sufficient representation-preserving inequalities $a_i\geq\delta_i$, $c_i\geq\rho_i$. The residual remains in the same nef cone, its order gap is $\sum_i(R_i(\theta)-R_i(\beta))\geq0$, and equality holds exactly when every initially $H_i$-active block retains $a_i-\delta_i+b_i>0$ and every initially $Q_i$-only block retains $c_i-\rho_i+d_i>0$. Example~26.19.1, printed p.~1181 gives genuinely nonclosed positive $\theta_t=tH+gQ$ and residual $(t-s)H+(g+s)Q$ after removal of $sE$, $0\leq s\leq t$. Equality holds for $s<t$, while $s=t$ gives jump $\ell+1$, realizing every integer from one to the dimension minus one. The chosen boundary current has actual divisorial mass, although perturbative minimal divisorial multiplicities remain zero.\par Book, Proposition~26.19.11, printed p.~1181 removes the constant-rank requirement in this comparison. For a smooth closed semipositive $B$, put $R=\max_X\operatorname{rank}B$. The full quotient comparison and closed intersection polynomial give the same two-sided $\epsilon^{n-R}$ bounds: $B^{R+1}=0$, and the top nonzero mixed coefficient is positive on a nonempty open set. The target background is still nef, the ambient manifold is K\"ahler, and the lower comparison still requires its global $L^1$ potential. Corollary~26.19.2, printed p.~1182 applies to any finite collection of smooth closed semipositive generators $B_j$ with fixed strictly positive smooth $f_j$ and parameters $t_j\geq0$: $\theta=\sum_jt_jf_jB_j$. Its order is $n-\max_X\operatorname{rank}(\sum_{t_j>0}B_j)$, including the empty active set. It preserves this order and the power bounds under every modification with compact K\"ahler manifold source, using only smooth pulled-back comparisons. The actual rank of the sum accounts for overlapping generators; constants are not asserted uniform across parameter faces. Example~26.19.2, printed p.~1183 gives nonclosed $(f\circ p_2)p_1^*(b\omega_1)$ on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^q$, with $f>0$ nonconstant, $b\geq0$ nonzero and zero on an open set, and exact order $q$. Thus the closed generators themselves may have open zero-rank regions.\par A smooth compact connected anticanonical curve $D$ with $D^2=0$ in a complex surface has a unitary flat divisor line on a neighborhood (Book, Theorem~26.19.3, printed p.~1186). The complete local proof uses a holonomy-independent flat elliptic inverse and a weighted fiberwise contraction; no arithmetic condition on the degree-zero normal line is imposed. A concave logarithmic cutoff gives a smooth closed semipositive divisor curvature $B$, supported in an annulus, of rank at most one (Book, Proposition~26.19.12, printed p.~1188). On a compact K"ahler surface its maximum rank is exactly one, because $\int_SB\wedge\kappa=\int_D\kappa>0$. Every fixed smooth $f>0$ therefore gives a nef background $fB$ with two-sided variational-volume bounds by $\epsilon$ for arbitrary Hermitian perturbation and smooth positive probability; choices with $\mathrm df\wedge B\ne0$ are nonclosed (Book, Corollary~26.19.3, printed p.~1189). For the closed perturbation, $\mathcal V_\mu(B+\epsilon\kappa)=2\epsilon\int_D\kappa+\epsilon^2\int_S\kappa^2$. Nine successive blowups along the strict transforms of a smooth plane cubic, including infinitely near centers, give these anticanonical square-zero curves (Book, Proposition~26.19.13, printed p.~1190). The anticanonical line is semiample exactly when its elliptic normal line is torsion; exact order $m$ gives the first moving, basepoint-free system $|mD|$. For a non-torsion normal line every $|kD|$ is the singleton $\{kD\}$, yet the smooth rank-one semipositive curvature and nonclosed order-one multiples still exist. Thus the comparison class includes geometric generators that have no generated positive tensor power.\par The flat neighborhood also controls the divisor complement. For a smooth compact connected divisor in a complex manifold of dimension at least two, a flat divisor line gives compact Levi-flat circle levels. A torsion normal line of exact order $m$ gives a proper local holomorphic function with divisor $mD$ and connected compact nonzero fibers (Book, Proposition~26.19.14, printed p.~1192). A non-torsion normal line has dense Levi leaves; maximum modulus forces every holomorphic function on a punctured tube to be constant. Thus every compact-hole complement that is connected has only constant holomorphic functions, which extend to the full divisor complement (Book, Theorem~26.19.4, printed p.~1192). For either holonomy regime the complement is not Stein; in particular the non-torsion nine-point cubic example has the Hartogs property and only constant global holomorphic functions (Book, Corollary~26.19.4, printed p.~1193). These complement results retain the flat-neighborhood hypothesis and do not supply a comparator for a general nonclosed nef background.
formal_entries.gap: No unrestricted common-order or integrality assertion survives the examples. Find hypotheses on geometry, torsion, or the degenerating positive representatives that force the closed-type behavior, and characterize equality in the comparison inequalities. These results fix strictly positive coefficient functions and specified closed semipositive generators or global current comparisons. Their divisor inequalities are sufficient for the displayed residual representation and do not characterize every nef residual or alternative cone representation. Fixed functions that vanish and modifications with non-Kahler source remain outside the proved regime. The maximum-rank criterion also requires a closed semipositive comparator and its stated global current comparison. It does not classify backgrounds without such a comparator or arbitrary vanishing coefficient functions. The generator corollary pulls back only smooth comparisons, so it makes no assertion about pulling back a general $L^1$ potential. The flat-divisor construction adds a geometric family within this comparison criterion; it does not provide a comparator for an arbitrary nonclosed nef background or classify all compact complex surfaces.

formal_entries.label: conj:lck-lee-psef
formal_entries.text:
\label{conj:lck-lee-psef}
For every compact strictly LCK manifold, the ordinary Bott--Chern class $\{\kappa_\lambda\}$ is pseudoeffective.
formal_entries.state: Constant least relative Lee-curvature eigenvalue forces it to be zero and yields a semipositive nonzero nef ordinary Bott--Chern class. The sufficient criterion excludes balanced metrics and covers invariant tensors on existing compact quotients. Two explicit all-dimensional Hopf families separate constant minimum from constant spectrum and retain positive first-boundary volume despite indefinite Lee curvature. General P03 remains open.
formal_entries.gap: Remove the constant-minimum hypothesis; prove nonnegative pairing with every Gauduchon test or find a strictly LCK counterexample. Indefinite curvature alone and degeneration at only some points do not settle the conjecture.

formal_entries.label: q:lck-gauduchon-volume
formal_entries.text:
\label{q:lck-gauduchon-volume}
Does a compact LCK manifold have at most one Gauduchon LCK metric with a specified Lee class, specified twisted Bott--Chern class and specified smooth positive volume form?
formal_entries.state: The coupled system is derived in Chapter 29. Ordinary Hermitian Monge--Amp\`ere uniqueness does not impose the second equation or preserve the twisted class. A prescribed-volume theorem is available in the Vaisman setting for volume forms invariant under both Lee and anti-Lee vector fields; it supplies a restricted existence and uniqueness result. For the scalar Hopf manifold $H_n=(\mathbb C^n\setminus\{0\})/\langle z\mapsto\mathrm e z\rangle$, $n\geq2$, let $r=\log|z|^2$ modulo two, $m=n-1$, $\alpha=\ddc r$ and $\beta=\mathrm dr\wedge\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}r$. Among all smooth positive radial metrics $\omega=C(r)\alpha+D(r)\beta$, Theorem~29.4.2, printed p.~1446, proves existence and metric uniqueness for every positive smooth two-periodic density $F=C^mD$ and every Lee period $L_0<0$, with radial orientation given by increasing $r$. Its periodic ODE is $C^mC^{\prime}=kC+F$, $k<0$; the uniquely selected constant has $L_0=-\int_0^2F/C^{m+1}\,\mathrm dr$. Proposition~29.4.2, printed p.~1446, supplies a positive actual-gauge twisted potential and zero twisted Bott--Chern class. The corresponding coupled-system uniqueness holds among radial metric candidates even if their smooth difference potential is not radial. Proposition~29.4.3, printed p.~1447, shows that every nonconstant $F$ gives a non-Vaisman metric; Example~29.4.1, printed p.~1447, gives an explicit such family. These are restricted partial results, not uniqueness among arbitrary LCK metrics.
formal_entries.gap: Prove that the coupled system determines the metric in the full LCK setting, including arbitrary nonradial candidates on the scalar Hopf manifold. The radial periodic classification does not prove that a general solution must be radial, or settle arbitrary twisted classes or compact LCK geometries. Uniqueness of a function $u$ is stronger and must account for the kernel of $D_\lambda$. Ordinary-potential examples with degenerate densities do not answer this smooth positive twisted problem.

formal_entries.label: conj:lck-calabi-yau-vaisman
formal_entries.text:
\label{conj:lck-calabi-yau-vaisman}
A compact complex manifold with $c_1^{\mathrm{BC}}(X)=0$ that admits a strictly LCK metric admits a Vaisman metric.
formal_entries.state: A Gauduchon LCK metric which is also Chern--Ricci flat is Vaisman by the rigidity result reconstructed in Book, Theorem~29.5.1. Vanishing $c_1^{\mathrm{BC}}$ gives a Chern--Ricci-flat conformal representative; Gauduchon's theorem gives a Gauduchon representative. These two representatives need not coincide. The Vaisman volume theorem retains the invariance hypotheses on the prescribed volume. Theorem~29.5.1, printed p.~1448 proves for every fixed Chern--Ricci-flat strictly LCK metric that $\int|S^-|^2=\frac12\int|\mathrm d^*\lambda|^2$. Here all norms and volumes use that metric, and $S^-$ is the anti-$J$-invariant part of $\nabla\lambda$. For that metric, the Gauduchon condition, zero Lee divergence, holomorphicity of the Lee field and the Vaisman condition are equivalent. Example~29.5.1, printed p.~1450 constructs one fixed Kodaira surface with trivial canonical bundle, a non-Gauduchon strictly LCK flat metric and an explicit Vaisman metric in its conformal class. The only flat representatives in that class are positive constant multiples, so none is Gauduchon. This obstructs a simultaneous conformal gauge, but the surface already admits a Vaisman metric and is not a counterexample to P05.

formal_entries.label: qu:hermitian-i-characterization
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:hermitian-i-characterization}
For a big nonclosed background on a manifold with bounded mass, find criteria for $\underline{\operatorname{vol}}_\theta(P_\theta[u]_{\mathcal I})>0$ in terms of restricted multiplier ideals or divisorial orders. When this lower volume vanishes, which implications between envelope equality and upper-volume equality in \cref{prop:conditional-i-characterization} remain valid?

formal_entries.label: qu:individual-equation-threshold
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:individual-equation-threshold}\index{Subsolution!exact threshold equation problem}
Suppose $v_-(h)=0$. For a nonzero $0\leq f\in L^1(\mathrm{d}V)$ with $b_h(f)>0$, does there exist $u\in\PSH(X,h)$ such that
\[
 \mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_h(u)=b_h(f)f\,\mathrm{d}V?
\]
Determine the singularity or envelope class in which such an equation should be posed.
formal_entries.state: Every positive threshold is attained by a subsolution, possibly with excess or infinite mass. For $L^p$ data, $p>1$, an exact continuous equation is available without positive lower mass. For all nonzero $L^1$ data when $v_-(h)>0$, an exact solution exists in the zero-reference relative envelope class, even without BMP. At positive individual threshold, greatest exponential solutions exist; their scalars approach $b_h(f)$ and their equation measures converge in total variation. Smooth positive or suitable smooth semipositive dual maximizers yield exactness and uniqueness. Moment bounds plus a genuine smaller-background envelope also yield an exact limit. For a zero-lower-mass factor times normalized $\mathbf P^k$, $k\geq1$, with split background, Theorem~14.29.1, printed p.~657, gives explicit probability densities in $L^1$ and in no $L^p$, $p>1$, whose threshold is $\binom{m+k}{m}\int h_0^m$. Their canonical pullbacks solve the exact finite-mass equation, belong to the zero-reference stretching class and admit every smaller-background envelope by actual competitors. Corollary~14.29.1, printed p.~659, gives the elliptic-threefold product with $\mathbf P^2$ and threshold $240\pi$. This settles the displayed density family; general P07 and exponential potential selection remain open. Theorem~14.29.2, printed p.~660 extends the exact finite-mass equation to every nonzero nonnegative integrable density from any normalized compact K\"ahler factor of dimension at least two. For $H=h_0+\kappa$, $N=m+k$, $c_0=\binom Nm\int h_0^m$, $\mu=(\int h_0^m)^{-1}h_0^m\wedge\kappa^k$ and $R=\mu/\mathrm dV$, the density $Rg$ has threshold $c_0/\int_Yg\kappa^k$ and an exact solution pulled back from $Y$. Neither boundedness below nor higher $L^p$ integrability is required. If the base has zero lower mass, the product does too. The general density on the product and exponential potential selection remain open. For $n\geq3$, Theorem~14.32.1, printed p.~675 gives a sufficient condition on a fixed datum: if $\int_Ef\,\mathrm dV\leq A\operatorname{Cap}_h(E)^{1+\alpha}$ for all Borel $E$, with $A,\alpha>0$, then $0<b_h(f)<\infty$, $f^{1/n}\in\mathcal D_h^0$, and normalized clipped solutions have a uniformly convergent subsequence solving $\mathrm{MA}_h(\phi)=b_h(f)f\,\mathrm dV$ with $\phi$ continuous. For every $0\leq g\leq f$ of positive integral, $b_h(g)\geq C(\int_Xg\,\mathrm dV)^{-\alpha/(1+\alpha)}$ and $\rho_h(g^{1/n})\leq C'(\int_Xg\,\mathrm dV)^{\alpha/(n(1+\alpha))}$. Theorem~14.32.2, printed p.~677 constructs such a logarithmic density on each fixed Hermitian background, including one of zero lower mass, with $b_h(f)=1$, no $L^p$ integrability for any $p>1$, and $\rho_h(f^{1/n}\mathbf1_{\{f>K\}})\leq C(\log K)^{-\alpha}$. The capacity bound is an additional hypothesis; neither general S04 question nor general P07 is settled. No homogeneous potential uniqueness or selection of the greatest exponential family is inferred.
formal_entries.gap: For general $L^1$ data at zero lower mass, construct an exact finite-mass solution and identify its natural class. Scalar and measure convergence alone do not imply capacity convergence of normalized potentials. Root tails, dual attainment, and envelope genuineness are separate hypotheses.

formal_entries.label: thm:radial-positive-volume-nonbig
formal_entries.text:
\label{conj:nef-gaud-volume-big}\index{Gauduchon variational volume!bigness conjecture}
Let $\theta$ be a nef smooth real $(1,1)$-background on a compact complex manifold. Then
\[
 \mathcal V_\mu(\theta)>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \theta\text{ is big}.
\]
Here $\mu$ is any smooth strictly positive probability measure.
formal_entries.current_resolution: resolved negatively in original unrestricted scope; counterexamples for n>=3
formal_entries.state: The unrestricted original equivalence is false. Book, Theorem~26.13.1, printed p.~1123 constructs, for every $n\geq3$, a smooth semipositive nef nonclosed background on $\mathbb P^{n-1}\times\mathbb P^1$ that is not big and has $\mathcal V_\mu(\theta)=n$. Put $m=n-1$, $t=(m-1)/m$, $x=\sum_{j=1}^m|Z_j|^2/\sum_{j=0}^m|Z_j|^2$, $a=x/t$ and $\theta=\omega+a w$, with normalized Fubini--Study forms and $\mu=\omega^m\wedge w$. Book, Lemma~26.13.1, printed p.~1121 gives the global bounded canonical radial potential by uniform smooth approximation, including the finite zero and every infinity chart. Its off-fiber determinant gives a lower bound against every smooth positive Gauduchon test; explicit smooth balanced metrics attain the matching perturbed quotients. A localized closed base-top-degree test excludes every strict quasi-psh current representative. Bigness still implies positive root volume. In dimension one the converse is the integral criterion; for closed nef classes on compact K\"ahler manifolds it is the classical nef-and-big criterion. The closed positive-volume core remains a sufficient condition. Positivity is independent of the chosen smooth positive probability. The result is independently reconstructed from the author's supplied source; it is not a priority or classification claim.
formal_entries.gap: No unresolved part of the original unrestricted equivalence remains: its forward implication is proved and its reverse implication is false. Separate followups concern nef nonclosed surface backgrounds, closed nef classes on general compact complex manifolds (P09), additional geometric criteria. P12 realizes the radial background, up to a smooth gauge change, at the maximal time of an actual Chern--Ricci flow and refutes that proposed endpoint implication too. Taking an infimum over all smooth probability densities would change the invariant and does not repair the original conjecture.

formal_entries.label: qu:closed-nef-gaud-bridge
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:closed-nef-gaud-bridge}
Let $\alpha$ be closed and nef with $\int_X\alpha^n>0$. Prove a positive lower bound for $\lambda_\mu(\alpha)$, and rule out the collapse in \cref{prop:gaud-positive-volume-collapse} for a sequence minimizing the bigness threshold of $\alpha$.
formal_entries.state: Both bridges hold on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Guedj--Lu prove, under the stated nefness and positive intersection assumptions, bigness if and only if bounded upper mass holds. The book describes collapse of determinant denominators along threshold-minimizing Gauduchon tests. Neither its Hopf BMP counterexample nor its zero-lower-mass elliptic threefold provides a counterexample to the classical conjecture: neither carries the required closed nef class with positive top intersection. The radial counterexample resolving P08 has a nonclosed background and leaves both closed bridges separate.
formal_entries.gap: Prove a strictly positive Gauduchon root-volume bound from the closed intersection, then control the determinant denominator along at least one sequence minimizing the strict-current threshold. Prescribing a volume within an Aeppli class preserves the closed numerator but does not control trace normalization and denominator together.

formal_entries.label: qu:geometric-gaud-endpoint
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:geometric-gaud-endpoint}
Find geometric conditions beyond the metric identities in \cref{cor:geometric-determinant-bound} that imply the endpoint estimate in \eqref{eq:pvp-endpoint-geometric}, and identify how they exclude the lower-mass degeneration of \cref{sec:vanishing-lower-mass}.
formal_entries.state:
The manuscript proves the exact equivalence
\[v_-(h)>0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \sup_{T\in\mathscr G_h}\|k_T\|_{L^{n/(n-1)}(\mathrm dV)}<\infty,\quad
 \sup\|k_T\|_{n/(n-1)}=v_-(h)^{-1/n}.\]
Every strictly smaller exponent is uniformly controlled on arbitrary compact complex manifolds. The endpoint holds if a metric's first two powers are $\ddc$-closed, including K\"ahler manifolds and compact complex surfaces. A balanced BMP threefold has zero lower mass and violates the endpoint even for smooth positive tests. Theorem~26.16.1, printed p.~1135, gives a geometric sufficient condition for principal elliptic threefolds over K\"ahler surfaces: the sum of the squares of the real curvature forms is nonnegative and nonzero. The bounded cubic identity gives the exact positive lower mass of the split metric and the endpoint for the full normalized current family in every Hermitian background. These manifolds have no pluriclosed metric. Proposition~26.16.2, printed p.~1137, constructs negative-line-bundle quotients with nonzero second real cohomology; Proposition~26.16.3, printed p.~1138, constructs a Calabi--Eckmann family without LCK metrics. Proposition~26.16.1, printed p.~1136, identifies the opposite sign for primitive curvature pairs.
formal_entries.gap: The nonnegative curvature-pair criterion settles the stated principal elliptic threefold families. Find further geometric conditions, including changing-sign curvature, primitive elliptic bundles and higher-dimensional geometries. Balancedness plus BMP is insufficient. A bounded determinant density for one smooth maximizer gives no bound for all tests or all near-maximizing sequences.

formal_entries.label: prob:primitive-elliptic-lower-mass
formal_entries.text:
\label{prob:primitive-elliptic-lower-mass}
Determine the lower Monge--Amp\`ere mass of the primitive elliptic bundles
above, in particular those of \cref{ex:primitive-elliptic-k3}.
Does it vanish whenever the real Chern class is nonzero?
formal_entries.state:
The metric is balanced, $\ddc\omega=-\pi^*(c^2)\geq0$, and $v_+(\omega)=3TA$. Its smooth mass satisfies
\[\int_X(\omega+\ddc u)^3=3TA-3\int_X\mathrm du\wedge\mathrm d^cu\wedge(-\pi^*c^2).\]
If the real Chern class vanishes, the chosen metric is K\"ahler and $v_-=3TA$. For nonzero Chern class, separated potentials $f(t)+\pi^*v$ have a uniform positive mass lower bound; the purely vertical subclass has an explicitly computed positive infimum. A bundle over $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ has zero lower mass by a construction outside that subclass. The K3 example has no divisors and only vertical compact curves. Transverse concentration now has an all-test criterion: if the normalized smooth strictly positive $\ddc$-closed complementary tests have uniformly bounded pairings with a transverse approximate identity along some shrinking sequence, the inner local hypersurface lies in a global analytic hypersurface (Theorem~4.5.1, printed p.~170). Thus these pairings diverge on the divisor-free K3 bundle. A multiplicity-one Cartier divisor agreeing throughout the cutoff chart gives the converse uniform bound by smooth logarithmic regularizations (Proposition~4.5.1, printed p.~170). For the specified family $\Gamma=a(t)\eta^2+g(t)\eta\wedge D$, where $D=\mathrm dt\wedge\mathrm d^ct$, strict positivity and $\ddc$-closure are equivalent to constant $a>0$ and $g>0$. With $V=3TA$, $\bar g=T^{-1}\int_0^Tg(t)\,\mathrm dt$ and $d_\Gamma=TA(a+\bar g)$, its positive root has volume $R=\frac32TA\sqrt a\,\bar g\leq d_\Gamma^{3/2}/\sqrt V$, with equality exactly when $\bar g=2a$, even for nonconstant $g$ (Proposition~33.3.3, printed p.~1608). Hence concentrating radial coefficients in this family have bounded root volume at fixed degree.
formal_entries.gap: Determine the infimum over all bounded admissible potentials, in particular on the K3 example. Decide whether every nonzero real Chern class forces zero lower mass. A positive bound for separated potentials gives no answer, and horizontal curve averaging cannot be transferred to the curve-free base. Divergent transverse pairings do not imply divergent positive-root volumes, and the radial bound controls only the displayed family. Neither result constructs a sequence of potentials with masses tending to zero or bounds all admissible potentials.

formal_entries.label: thm:actual-flow-positive-volume-nonbig
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:chern-ricci-gaud-singularities}
Suppose a Chern--Ricci flow has finite maximal time $\tau$ and $\mathcal V_\mu(\theta_\tau)>0$. Can one prove that $\theta_\tau$ is big and that the flow converges smoothly to a positive metric locally on $X\setminus E_{\mathrm{nH}}(\theta_\tau)$, without a bounded mass hypothesis? How do the annihilating Gauduchon currents describe the resulting degeneracy?
formal_entries.state: The original first implication is false. Book, Theorem~26.20.3, printed p.~1217 constructs an actual smooth Chern--Ricci flow on $\mathbb P^{n-1}\times\mathbb P^1$, for every $n\geq3$, with finite maximal book time $\tau=1/(2\pi)$ and a nef nonbig limiting background of exact fixed-density volume $n$. With the radial notation of P08, take $\omega_0=(n+1)\omega+(a+2)w$. Its endpoint is $\theta+\ddc\log(a+2)$, so smooth gauge invariance transfers the full Gauduchon volume and all-potential nonbigness obstruction. Strict reference representatives exist at every earlier time, and a closed base-top-degree test excludes even pseudoeffectivity at later times; the book's maximal-time theorem supplies the actual flow. Book, Proposition~26.20.2, printed p.~1218 shows that every normalized endpoint annihilator has trace supported on $Z=\{p\}\times\mathbb P^1$ and vertical rank-one matrix. The explicit current is $[Z]/2$, and each annihilator satisfies $\int_X\omega(s)\wedge R=1-2\pi s$. This is an averaged trace, not pointwise metric collapse. Dang's qualitative null-locus equality and parabolic convergence theorem retain their nef-big or big endpoint hypotheses. The separate flow theorem using positive limiting lower volume retains the surface or Guan--Li assumptions.
formal_entries.gap: The unrestricted bigness implication is settled negatively, so the original proposed general conclusion cannot hold. Further directions concern additional conditions ensuring a big endpoint, geometric degeneration of actual evolving metrics, and analytic support for annihilators at other endpoints. In this model support follows from strict positivity of the semipositive representative away from one fiber; determinant vanishing alone still gives no general support theorem. Conditional smooth convergence off a big endpoint's non-Hermitian locus remains available from the cited theorem. Metric completeness and simultaneous nefness/smoothing compatibility remain separate refinements of S13. No surface counterexample, weak continuation or unconditional local convergence is asserted.
formal_entries.current_resolution: Negatively resolved: actual nonbig positive-volume flow endpoint for every n>=3

formal_entries.label: qu:balanced-pluriclosed-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:balanced-pluriclosed-program}
Use the coexistence of a balanced metric and a pluriclosed metric to construct closed positive data, or to control a geometric flow that can change the torsion. Determine what estimate beyond the finite balanced trace prevents metric degeneration. Can determinant estimates for Gauduchon currents contribute to that estimate?
formal_entries.state: If a single metric is both balanced and pluriclosed, it is already K\"ahler. The book proves this implication directly in Lemma~33.3.3. Chen--Zheng resolve the coexistence question when there is a real connection $D$ and a Hermitian metric $g$ with $Dg=DJ=DT^D=0$: the two given metrics may differ from $g$, and the conclusion is a $D$-parallel K\"ahler metric (Book, Theorem~33.3.1). The proof uses a strictly positive projection onto parallel forms, commuting with exterior differentiation, followed by a volume maximum on a positive affine slice of fixed pointwise trace. Parallelism makes the slice bounded and every boundary form singular everywhere; these pointwise conclusions do not follow from a general integral trace bound. A pluriclosed manifold in Fujiki's class is K\"ahler by Chiose, so producing a closed K\"ahler current would suffice. The balanced form supplies a conserved trace in the cited invariant flow examples. Scalar potential perturbations preserve torsion: $\mathrm d(\omega+\ddc u)=\mathrm d\omega$; a prescribed-volume equation cannot supply closedness. Conditional deformation stability is also known: for a smooth family of integrable complex structures on a compact manifold with locally constant $h_A^{1,1}$, any prescribed initial pluriclosed metric extends to a smooth family of pluriclosed metrics (Book, Theorem~33.3.2, printed p.~1616). Lemma~33.3.4, printed p.~1615, constructs the smoothly varying closed-form projection. Positivity follows near the initial strict metric by continuity. The construction supplies neither the balanced companion nor closedness or Bismut flatness, so it leaves the coexistence and flow questions open. Theorem~26.17.1, printed p.~1143 computes the complete normalized Gauduchon-current profile when $\ddc(\beta^j)=0$ for $1\leq j\leq n-1$: for every $p\in L^n(\mathrm dV)$ its supremum is $V^{-1/n}\|p\|_n$, where $V=\int_X\beta^n$. Singular and degenerate currents are retained, and the intrinsic determinant measures and actual current sets are unchanged by positive smooth scalar-potential perturbations. Theorem~26.17.2, printed p.~1145 and Theorem~26.17.3, printed p.~1146 give closed and nonclosed pluriclosed torus families with identical complete determinant data, fixed positive bounded-potential mass extrema and uniformly bounded smooth coefficients, while the least relative eigenvalue tends to zero. The nonclosed family retains fixed nonzero torsion and a separate balanced metric on an already K\"ahler torus. Theorem~26.17.4, printed p.~1147 gives exact maximizers for varying unit $L^n$ roots, uniformly convergent continuous potentials, and critical determinant-power densities that are not uniformly integrable. The limiting current has zero intrinsic determinant measure while its bounded potential has positive Monge--Amp\`ere mass. This is a partial limitation result for the scalar data; it proves neither the coexistence conjecture nor an estimate along an actual flow.
formal_entries.gap: Produce closed positive data from the coexistence of the two metrics, or obtain flow estimates controlling torsion and pointwise ellipticity. A finite conserved balanced trace alone does not prevent metric degeneration. Determine whether Gauduchon determinant bounds help supply the missing local estimate. The fixed-profile examples show that the complete scalar determinant data, positive mass extrema and smooth coefficient bounds alone cannot yield a positive uniform lower eigenvalue bound. Additional geometric-flow information or pointwise hypotheses are required; no flow trajectory, convergence theorem or fixed-density exact maximizing sequence is supplied.
formal_entries.source: \cite[Conjectures 1.1 and 1.2]{FV26}; \cite[Theorem 0.2 in the author manuscript]{Chiose14}; \cite[v1, Theorem 1.2; Lemmas 3.1--3.2 and Propositions 3.3--3.5; Propositions 4.2 and 4.5 and Lemmas 4.3--4.4]{CZParallel26}; \cite[v5, Theorem~8.11, Section~8.3, p.~41]{CavSKT13}; \cite[v1, Section~2.c, pp.~9--10]{SchAeppli07}; \cite[v1, Theorem~2.1, p.~7]{BarDef26}; Chapter 33, closed positivity section. Book, Theorem~26.17.1, printed p.~1143; Theorem~26.17.2, printed p.~1145; Theorem~26.17.3, printed p.~1146; Theorem~26.17.4, printed p.~1147; smooth existence input \cite[arXiv v2, Corollary~1, p.~1; final existence-reference paragraph p.~8]{TW10}.

formal_entries.label: qu:hermitian-morse-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:hermitian-morse-program}
Find geometric hypotheses controlling the cost in \eqref{eq:gaud-volume-subtraction-cost} up to a nef endpoint beyond the closed-core regime of \cref{thm:closed-core-subtraction}. Determine when positive root volume forces bigness without that core. For closed backgrounds, compare the estimate with classical Morse inequalities; for nonclosed backgrounds, retain the differential data and the dependence on $\mu$.
formal_entries.state: First variation proves the identity on positive compact segments without an upper mass bound. A closed nef positive-volume core plus a semipositive summand gives an endpoint estimate and a strict current. In the closed K\"ahler setting, the cited transcendental Morse inequality bounds the usual class volume by $\int\alpha^n-n\int\alpha^{n-1}\beta$; volume differentiability and cone duality are retained as literature inputs. For $X=B\times C$, with a compact K\"ahler base of dimension $m\geq2$, a curve, specified product probability $\mu=\sigma\wedge w$, and $\theta_s=\alpha+(a+t-s)w$ for any smooth $a\geq0$, Book, Theorem~26.12.1, printed p.~1117 computes the full variational volume and the cost for every minimizer: $\mathcal V_\mu(\theta_s)=nW/H(t-s)$ and $\mathcal C(s)=n^{-(n-1)/n}W^{1/n}H(t-s)^{-(n+1)/n}J(t-s)$, where $n=m+1$, $W=\int_B\alpha^m$, $H(\epsilon)=\int_B\sigma/(a+\epsilon)$ and $J(\epsilon)=\int_B\sigma/(a+\epsilon)^2$. The improper integral is finite and equals the actual root-volume drop, even when $H(0)=+\infty$ and the endpoint volume is zero. Book, Proposition~26.12.1, printed p.~1119 gives the five cost rates determined by real zero codimension $d$ and order $k$, with positive endpoint volume exactly when $d>k$. Book, Proposition~26.12.2, printed p.~1120 proves that the endpoint is big exactly when $a>0$ everywhere; any zero excludes every closed nef core of positive top self-intersection, including after smooth gauge. The constant closed case attains the classical Morse expression, while nonconstant $a$ retains the prescribed density and torsion.
formal_entries.gap: Control the cost near arbitrary nef endpoints without the closed core and obtain a criterion making positive root volume imply bigness. For nonclosed forms, ordinary intersection expressions need not be invariant under smooth gauge. An estimate must specify its volume, retain torsion terms such as $\ddc$ of the added form, and state its dependence on $\mu$. The negative P08 resolution rules out an unconditional positive-volume bigness criterion for nef nonclosed backgrounds in dimension at least three; a geometric criterion must exclude that obstruction. The warped calculation does not control arbitrary nonproduct paths or characterize when positive root volume implies bigness outside the closed-core regime.

formal_entries.label: qu:gaud-metric-boundary
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:gaud-metric-boundary}
For a specified finite-dimensional cone of smooth background classes, describe the metric completion of its unit-volume hypersurface. Which boundary points admit a current representative, and what estimates on the minimizing Gauduchon metrics distinguish finite from infinite distance?
formal_entries.status: partially resolved for invariant and warped background cones; general question open
formal_entries.state: Homogeneity gives an isometry $(\mathscr C,g)\simeq(\mathbb R\times\mathscr S,\mathrm dr^2+g_{\mathscr S})$ with $r=\log\lambda$. Thus paths with volume tending to zero or infinity have infinite length. The product cone on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ is complete; the blowup of $\mathbb P^2$ has a finite-distance positive-nef-volume boundary. For a compact complex Lie-group quotient, a normalized invariant probability and a fixed real linear subspace $W\subset\operatorname{Herm}(n)$ containing a positive matrix, Book, Theorem~26.5.1, printed p.~1046 proves that $\mathscr S=\{A>0:H\det A=1\}$ is complete and proper. Its Cauchy sequences are exactly coefficient sequences converging to a positive matrix. Book, Proposition~26.5.2, printed p.~1043 identifies the normalized minimizing form as $\gamma_A=\theta_A/(H\det A)^{1/n}$ and characterizes positive-current coefficient classes by $A\geq0$. Spectral bounds control $\gamma_A$ pointwise. A nonzero singular coefficient limit becomes infinitely distant after normalization. In the full Iwasawa cone, Book, Example~26.5.2, printed p.~1048 gives the exact logarithmic matrix distance and the explicit rate $\sqrt2|\log\varepsilon|/3$ for $\operatorname{diag}(1,1,\varepsilon)$ after normalization. Book, Theorem~26.5.2, printed p.~1051 extends the determinant formula and the same complete prescribed coefficient metric on the Iwasawa quotient to every smooth probability invariant along its central elliptic fibers. These are exactly the smooth probabilities maximizing the volume of each invariant positive background. The minimizing metric is obtained from a closed base equation for the Schur complement; its coefficient mean retains the spectral distance bounds, without a claimed pointwise order estimate for the varying form. Book, Proposition~26.5.3, printed p.~1050 identifies the upper mass of every invariant threefold positive background as $H\det A$. Book, Corollary~26.5.1, printed p.~1050 gives zero non-pluripolar top mass for all plurisubharmonic potentials of singular semipositive invariant coefficients in dimension three. Book, Theorem~26.5.3, printed p.~1054 computes the full reciprocal-integral volume and actual balanced minimizers on the entire three-dimensional warped cone on a compact K\"ahler $m$-fold times a curve, with $m\geq2$ and its specified product probability. Book, Proposition~26.5.4, printed p.~1055 gives global Euclidean unit-surface coordinates. Book, Lemma~26.5.2, printed p.~1057 identifies its endpoint length with the reciprocal-coefficient trace variance of the minimizing tests: under finite disjoint two-sided power-stratum hypotheses, an end is finite exactly when its minimum real-codimension/vanishing-order ratio exceeds one. Book, Theorem~26.5.4, printed p.~1058 classifies every Cauchy point as a closed strip, closed half-plane or complete plane. Each finite end has a smooth semipositive nef nonbig representative of full variational volume one, with nonbigness proved against all singular strict current representatives. Book, Example~26.5.3, printed p.~1064 gives an explicit $\mathbb P^2$ product strip and Book, Example~26.5.4, printed p.~1065 an explicit complete torus plane with periodic base potentials. \par Book, Proposition~26.5.5, printed p.~1059 determines the full pseudoeffective, nef and strict-current cones in that same real span using localized closed tests on arbitrary quasi-plurisubharmonic current representatives. Book, Proposition~26.5.6, printed p.~1060 gives a continuous pulled-back potential solving the smooth positive prescribed-volume equation at every finite power-stratum unit-volume face. The base reciprocal density is in $L^p$ for every $1<p<r$, where $r>1$ is the endpoint codimension-to-order ratio. The bounded product equals the fixed probability, but no solution is globally $C^{1,1}$: bounded coefficients and the positive determinant would force a strict current representative excluded by the cone test. The obstruction is the general determinant-to-current bound in Book, Proposition~1.7.3, printed p.~41. Book, Proposition~26.5.7, printed p.~1061 proves uniform whole-sequence convergence of the constructed normalized pulled-back potentials to every finite unit-volume face, weak convergence of all their ordinary bounded products and uniqueness among normalized bounded solutions pulled back from the base. Strong reciprocal-density convergence supplies the fixed-background compactness bound; closed-base uniqueness identifies all cluster potentials. For an arbitrary bounded pulled-back endpoint competitor, closed mass invariance and positivity exclude residual mass on the extreme set before uniqueness is applied. Uniqueness among arbitrary endpoint solutions, smoothness off the real extreme strata and pointwise convergence of minimizing balanced metrics remain unproved. \par Book, Proposition~26.5.8, printed p.~1062 gives the exact balanced-cofactor trace and its sharp threshold: for $r>2$ the whole cofactor sequence has a finite positive closed current limit; for $1<r<2$ its trace has order $\epsilon^{r-2}$, and for $r=2$ order $\log(1/\epsilon)$. Book, Proposition~26.5.9, printed p.~1063 identifies every trace-normalized current cluster for $1<r\leq2$ as the pullback of a base probability supported on the extreme components with minimal codimension-to-order ratio. A single extreme point gives whole-sequence convergence to its curve-fiber integration current. The smooth numerator and denominator have the same vanishing rate, while their quotient remains one. In the projective strip both ends are in this logarithmic regime. These conclusions concern the fixed product probability and power-stratum geometry; they do not determine a pointwise metric limit or enlarge the general completion theorem.
formal_entries.gap: Classify the unit-volume completion for other specified background cones and reference densities, together with their current representatives and minimizing-metric estimates. The general Lie-group result uses the invariant probability, while the larger fiber-invariant density family is proved specifically on the Iwasawa quotient. Densities varying along its central fibers have strictly smaller variational volume; their Hessian completion is not determined by that value inequality. Nonzero singular coefficient limits in the proved matrix families are infinitely distant after normalization, while a raw sequence tending to zero may normalize to an existing positive point. Adjoining all nef classes does not give the answer. Distances may shorten after enlarging the cone; no infinite-dimensional completion follows. The warped completion theorem fixes its product probability and excludes intersecting extreme strata and infinite-order zeros. Trace-moment estimates do not assert a pointwise limit of the minimizing metrics. Completion for other warped densities and extreme-set geometries remains open.

formal_entries.label: conj:continuous-gaud-adjoint
formal_entries.text:
\label{conj:continuous-gaud-adjoint}\index{Adjoint measure!continuous-density conjecture}
For a Hermitian background $\omega$, the nonsingular reference $\varphi=0$, and every real $F\in C(X)$, the set $\mathcal A_0(F)$ consists of a single probability measure.
formal_entries.state: Supporting sets are nonempty, convex, weakly compact and absolutely continuous. They are singletons for smooth $F$, for closed K\"ahler backgrounds by explicit normalization, and on a dense $G_\delta$ of $C(X)$ in every admissible fixed reference regime. In dimension at least two, all supports are exactly normalized determinant-weighted measures of maximizing Gauduchon currents. Their densities have uniform $L^q$ bounds for $1<q<n/(n-1)$ on bounded sets of $F$, and at the endpoint if lower mass is positive. A bounded solution whose complex Hessian is continuous and everywhere strictly positive gives a unique stationary support and the G\^ateaux derivative (Theorem~15.2.4, printed p.~709). The proof uses the continuous-coefficient Sobolev Fredholm statement of Lemma~4.9.1, printed p.~226, without a Dini modulus or a full real $C^2$ hypothesis. On $\mathbb P^1\times Y$, with any connected compact Hermitian $k$-fold $(Y,\kappa)$ of volume one, background $aw+b\kappa$ and logarithmic density $F=\log((k+1)Ab^k)$, where $b>0$ is smooth and $A>0$ is continuous with $\int Aw=a$, the scalar is one and the support is $(A/a)w\otimes\nu_\kappa$ (Proposition~15.2.3, printed p.~710). This includes a non-Dini, non-H\"older density on $\mathbb P^1$ times a Hopf surface (Example~15.2.1, printed p.~710).
formal_entries.gap: Show that all maximizers induce the same weighted probability for every continuous $F$, or find an exceptional density. This asks less than uniqueness of the maximizing current. Compactness and subcritical moment bounds alone do not imply uniqueness; near-maximizers can have unbounded higher determinant moments even with fixed smooth data. The new criterion does not show that every continuous density has a bounded solution with continuous strictly positive complex Hessian. Its product formula fixes the stated factor structure; the unconditional every-continuous-density conjecture remains open.

formal_entries.label: qu:singularity-topology-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:singularity-topology-program}\index{Singularity type!topology problem}
Extend the complete metrizable topology of \cref{thm:positive-model-complete-metric} on ordinary models beyond bounded mass and positive lower volume, retaining analytic closure exactly at the ideal models. Preserve the smooth-gauge and two-sided background compatibility of \cref{sec:model-background-comparison,sec:two-sided-model-backgrounds}, and treat background limits losing bigness or a uniform positive lower-volume bound. Recover the complete polar-variation topology of \cref{cor:curve-model-completeness} on all curve models, and determine whether the higher-dimensional extension is completely metrizable.
formal_entries.state: The full curve-map model theorem now permits critical fibers; fixed-weight ideal extension is distinct from the all-weight type correspondence. The full curve model theorem now allows every smooth base form of nonnegative area, including the zero-area singleton. A stated finite factor of degree d gives two normalizations whose ratio is d; pushforward to the original base can lose component data. Classical curve-target factorization is now proved internally, so the finite-factor metric applies to every compact surjective curve map. General higher-rank backgrounds and cross-background complete topology remain open. Finite curve pullback now commutes with ordinary and ideal envelopes below pulled-back obstacles. Polar metric and volume scale by degree; the original-base model subspace is closed and complete with a mass-preserving 1-Lipschitz averaging retraction that commutes with ideal projection. The cubic analytic example shows that this retraction need not be nearest. General higher-rank and cross-background topology remains open.

formal_entries.label: qu:exact-trace-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:exact-trace-program}
If $Y$ fails at least one of the two mass properties, can the Hermitian background $\Omega$ in \cref{thm:trace-profile-model-envelope} be chosen so that
\[
 \nu\bigl(\mathcal T_\Omega(u;Y)\circ\pi,E\bigr)
       =\tau_{Y,u}(E)
\]
for every prime divisor $E$ on every smooth modification $\pi$ of $Y$? If so, determine a background-compatible ordinary or ideal singularity class of this realization, and prove its addition and approximation properties.

formal_entries.label: qu:positive-system-recovery
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:positive-system-recovery}
For a smooth big background on a manifold without bounded mass, find a condition on a compatible Hermitian envelope system that forces recovery of its ideal type at every finite parameter. It should recover the positive limiting lower-volume criterion of \cref{thm:positive-volume-system-recovery} when bounded mass holds. Specify the invariant and uniform estimates that replace the finite upper-volume deficit, and their behavior under modifications.
formal_entries.state: The retraction produces the greatest realizable system below the original one and recovery is equivalent to survival of its ideal data. Under BMP and a smooth big background, positive limiting lower volume at the initial slice suffices; concavity propagates positivity to every finite slice. A finite upper-volume deficit gives stretches controlling divisorial orders. A zero-volume ruled-surface example shows nonrecovery even in a K\"ahler background. Theorem~25.6.1, printed p.~1026 gives a different sufficient condition on the scalar Hopf threefold with its standard background $h=\pi^*\kappa+\mathrm ds\wedge\dc s$, where $\pi:X\to\mathbb P^2$ and $s=\log|z|^2$. If every positive scalar slice is invariant under $E=\mathbb C/(\mathbb Z+2\pi\mathrm i\mathbb Z)$ and the initial transverse limiting model $\psi_a$ satisfies $\underline{\operatorname{vol}}_\kappa(\psi_a)>0$, the system is recovered at every finite parameter and every positive ambient Hermitian perturbation. Scalar invariance constructs the full compatible base system; preservation of the limiting ideals is a conclusion. Example~25.6.1, printed p.~1027 gives nonanalytic ideal data from infinitely many hyperplanes, with exact transverse lower and upper volumes $(1-\lambda(\tau))^2>0$. Proposition~16.2.1, printed p.~783 transports the recovery identity to exact pulled backgrounds. Proposition~13.3.1, printed p.~522 preserves extended measures and both ordinary-type volumes under exact pullback, including for nonclosed backgrounds and infinite masses. Smooth gauge transport preserves recovery, although the transported scalar slices need not remain invariant.
formal_entries.gap: Find a recovery criterion for general nonsymmetric compatible systems and arbitrary smooth big backgrounds with unbounded upper mass, specializing to the positive-volume theorem under BMP. The Hopf result requires both scalar fiber symmetry and positive transverse initial lower volume. Exact pullback may give degenerate perturbing forms and does not construct the full system indexed by every new Hermitian form upstairs. Gauge transport alone does not ensure survival of ideals. No uniform positive-volume bound at the cutoff follows from the finite-parameter theorem.
formal_entries.source: Book, Definition~25.2.1, printed p.~1016; Theorem~25.3.1, printed p.~1016; Theorem~30.5.3, printed p.~1483; Theorem~25.6.1, printed p.~1026; Example~25.6.1, printed p.~1027; Proposition~16.2.1, printed p.~783; Proposition~13.3.1, printed p.~522; Proposition~25.4.1, printed p.~1019.

formal_entries.label: qu:partial-kernel-lower-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:partial-kernel-lower-program}
Identify hypotheses on a weighted section series and its intrinsic growth dimension under which the partial Fubini--Study potentials attain the envelope lower bound and the normalized kernel measures converge. Relate the limiting measure to the Hermitian background while retaining the closed curvature and the growth dimension of the series.
formal_entries.state: The general upper-envelope bound is proved. A matching lower bound and kernel-measure convergence hold in the closed-curvature positive-mass setting with a K\"ahler modification, retaining its Jacobian and relative canonical bundle. Descended series on submersions give base-dimensional limits. Isolated-point conditions permit finite-codimension comparison; horizontal projective and explicit Hopf series give further exact limits. Hopf growth has degree $n-1$, so normalization by $m^n$ would discard its nonzero limit. An interior rational Newton polytope on a product of projective lines gives a complete sufficient-condition model when its affine hull has an integral offset, its smooth invariant logarithmic weight is strictly convex, and its sampling probability is smooth, strictly positive and invariant on the whole manifold. Book, Theorem~27.16.1, printed p.~1333 proves the specified growth-envelope lower bound, all finite $L^p$ convergence and weighted Bernstein--Markov. Book, Theorem~27.16.2, printed p.~1334 computes the positive relative-dimensional kernel limit as lattice volume lifted to real moment tori. It is independent of the invariant sampling probability. In lower dimension it is singular and differs from the ambient mixed envelope-curvature measure; in full dimension it equals the non-pluripolar top product. Book, Example~27.16.1, printed p.~1335 includes nonclosed smooth sampling and a rational map with indeterminacy. A critical divisor multiplier-ideal family on a product of projective lines has positive growth exponent $q$ and potentials converging to its actual ideal envelope, while its $q!m^{-q}$-normalized kernel measures have two different positive weak limits. Book, Theorem~27.17.1, printed p.~1337 computes $N_m=a_m(m+1)^q$, with $a_m=1$ in even and $2$ in odd degrees, and restores a single probability limit after division by $N_m$. Its selector has zero top non-pluripolar mass and its ideal family is not multiplicative. This shows that a growth exponent alone is insufficient outside the positive-mass convergence regime.\par An actual ideal selector at the two isolated base points of a pencil on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ gives a convergent non-multiplicative model. Book, Lemma~27.18.1, printed p.~1340 identifies its all-weight ideal and ordinary upper type classes for every genuine competitor. Theorem~27.18.1, printed p.~1342 computes the full ideal envelope for the specified compact logarithmic box and quadratic norm weight. Proposition~27.18.1, printed p.~1343 gives the entire three-band space and exact dimension $3m+1$. Theorem~27.18.2, printed p.~1344 proves a global potential lower bound, every finite $L^p$ convergence, uniform exponential convergence and an intrinsic positive measure limit of mass three. Additive error remains unbounded near each pole at every fixed degree $m\geq2$. The norm, box and sampling probability are fixed; this selector also has zero top non-pluripolar mass.
formal_entries.gap: Find intrinsic hypotheses producing enough sections with the full ideal constraints and controlling their measures. The Newton theorem specifies a growth-constrained target; it does not identify an arbitrary multiplier-ideal envelope. Boundary-touching polytopes, noninvariant data and general selected series remain outside its hypotheses. Preserve closed line-bundle curvature while relating the limit to a possibly nonclosed ambient background. No unqualified equality with the raw Hermitian Monge--Amp\`ere measure of the selecting weight follows from the upper bound. Require convergence of the normalized section counts for a finite weak kernel-measure limit, rather than merely an intrinsic growth exponent. The specific three-band pencil model does not establish a universal all-weight ideal/ordinary class identity or convergence for other compact sampling and arbitrary selected families.

formal_entries.label: qu:fiber-selected-approximation
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:fiber-selected-approximation}
Let $\pi:X\to B$ be a surjective holomorphic submersion of connected compact complex manifolds with connected fibers, where $B$ is K\"ahler of dimension $q\geq1$. Fix a Hermitian form $\omega$ on $X$, a holomorphic line bundle $A$ with a smooth Hermitian metric $h$ on $B$, and $\varphi\in\PSH(X,\omega)$. Set $\theta=c_1(A,h)$. For positive integers $m$, identify
\[
 V_m=H^0\bigl(X,\pi^*A^m\otimes\mathcal I(m\varphi)\bigr)
          \subseteq H^0(B,A^m)
\]
by holomorphic descent. Find geometric or analytic conditions that produce $\psi\in\PSH(B,\theta)$ of positive non-pluripolar mass such that, for all sufficiently large $m$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 W_m=H^0\bigl(B,A^m\otimes\mathcal I(m\psi)\bigr)\subseteq V_m,\\
 \dim V_m-\dim W_m=o(m^q).
 \end{gathered}
\]
Determine which features of the singularities of $\varphi$ along the fibers suffice for this approximation.

formal_entries.label: prob:growing-jets-localization
formal_entries.text:
\label{prob:growing-jets-localization}
Let $C$ be a connected compact Riemann surface, let $x\in C$, and let $(L,h)$ be a smooth Hermitian holomorphic line bundle whose curvature is semipositive and strictly positive on $C\setminus\{x\}$. Fix an integer $r\geq1$. Suppose that in a local coordinate $z$ centered at $x$ and a holomorphic frame $e$ one has
\[
 |e|_h^2=\mathrm{e}^{-\phi},\qquad
 \phi(z)=|z|^{2r}+O(|z|^{2r+1}).
\]
Let $\nu$ be a smooth positive volume form with local expression $a(z)\,\mathrm{d}A$ and $a(0)=1$, where $\mathrm{d}A$ is Euclidean area. For positive integers $m$, choose integers $q_m\to\infty$ with $q_m=o(m)$. Give
\[
 V_m=H^0(C,L^m\otimes\mathfrak m_x^{q_m})
\]
the norm $\|s\|^2=\int_C|s|_{h^m}^2\,\mathrm{d}\nu$, where $\mathfrak m_x$ is the ideal sheaf of $x$. Write $B_m=\sum_j|s_{m,j}|_{h^m}^2$ for an orthonormal basis $(s_{m,j})$ of $V_m$, with value zero when $V_m=0$. Determine the growth ranges of $q_m$ for which, for each fixed real $\tau$, every sequence of points $x_m$ in the coordinate neighborhood satisfying
\[
 m|z(x_m)|^{2r}=q_m/r+\tau\sqrt{q_m/r}
\]
obeys
\[
 \frac{\pi B_m(x_m)}{mr^2|z(x_m)|^{2r-2}}
 \longrightarrow
 \Phi(\tau):=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^{\tau}
                         \mathrm{e}^{-s^2/2}\,\mathrm{d}s.
\]
When this transition law fails, determine how further terms of the local weight change its center and scale.

formal_entries.label: qu:singular-space-equations-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:singular-space-equations-program}
Beyond the projective-cone constructions of \cref{sec:projective-cone-equations}, determine geometric and measure conditions on compact unibranch Hermitian spaces that give existence and uniqueness in specified singularity classes. Identify estimates ensuring finite mass, descent and continuity, and their behavior under common refinements.
formal_entries.state:
The appendix proves disk-test descent under modifications and compatibility of ordinary envelopes, constructs resolution-independent non-pluripolar products, and gives explicit equations on projective cones under stated inequalities on their data. Dang provides continuity for bounded solutions under additional hypotheses, notably a log-terminal setting. Pan constructs a Gauduchon metric on the regular locus uniformly comparable to the prescribed metric, with conformal uniqueness up to scale.
 In the explicitly assumed standard nodal small-resolution model, Book, Lemma~14.18.3 constructs a strict analytic barrier and Corollary~14.18.1 gives a bounded fixed-smooth-density equation by subsequential potential degeneration, with exact exceptional-area decay. Book, Lemma~14.18.4 computes the pushed-forward density: it is in $L^p$ precisely for $1\leq p<3$, has a weak $L^3$ endpoint and is not in $L^3$ when a node is present. The bounded potential descends, including for a nonclosed ambient background, and solves (Book, equation~14.52) on the singular space. When the pullback background is closed, Book, Theorem~14.18.2 proves uniqueness among bounded normalized solutions and convergence of the entire smooth perturbation family. These arguments do not establish continuity at a node or settle the general prescribed-class problem.\par For compact unibranch curves with finite bijective torus normalization, Book, Lemma~A.7.1, printed p.~1722 constructs a periodic Green function directly. Theorem~A.7.1, printed p.~1723 proves an equation in every prescribed finite logarithmic ordinary type of total pole weight $A<H$, for nonzero nonnegative normalization-side $L^p$ data with $p>1$. Here $H=\int_E\pi^*h$, $\beta_0$ is flat area probability on the normalization $E$, and $f\geq0$ is its data density. The proportionality constant is $(H-A)/\int f\beta_0$, the entire genuine type has mass $H-A$, and uniqueness includes initially rough competitors. Disk lifts give genuine descent, a continuous residual and extended-value continuity at the poles; all curve resolutions and refinements are biholomorphic to the normalization. The local-embedding background may pull back degenerately. Example~A.7.1, printed p.~1725 supplies a nonnormal projective cusp with genus-one normalization, background mass six and a weight-one pole of nonpluripolar mass five. Its normalization-side density is smooth and positive, but the downstairs density belongs to $L^r(h)$ exactly for $1\leq r<2$, with logarithmic divergence at $r=2$. This is a dimension-one sufficient condition; all curve backgrounds are closed.\par Book, Theorem~A.7.2, printed p.~1728 gives an exact endpoint for normalization-side densities with local form $C_0|z|^{-2}(\log(1/|z|))^{-\gamma}$, where $C_0>0$ and the density is smoothly and positively extended away from the chosen point. They are integrable exactly for $\gamma>1$ and lie outside every $L^p$, $p>1$. Within this family, a positive-proportionality equation has a solution in the prescribed ordinary logarithmic type exactly for $\gamma>2$; it is unique in that entire type and has a continuous residual with no positive H\"older exponent upstairs. For $1<\gamma\leq2$, a constructed genuine descended solution has the same mass $H-A$ and all-weight resolution multiplier ideals, but its residual is unbounded below. No ordinary-type solution exists, even with an unspecified positive proportionality constant. The proof uses a cutoff radial primitive and a smooth mean-zero Green correction; it retains the possibly degenerate background.\par In every dimension $n\geq2$, an explicit product of a cuspidal curve with square elliptic curves has a nonclosed local-embedding Hermitian background whose normalization admits a positive smooth reference repair and has all background powers $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm c}$-closed (Book, Proposition~A.8.1, printed p.~1731). Fix an integer $s\geq n+3$ before choosing its sufficiently small nonzero real perturbation. A quantitative contraction solves full-variable normalized densities in a small $H^s$ neighborhood of the positive reference density, with a $C^2$ normalization-side potential and solution form at least one quarter of the flat reference (Book, Theorem~A.8.1, printed p.~1732). Every bounded ordinary potential has the same mass, and a weighted decreasing-product limit gives uniqueness against all bounded competitors, including rough ones (Book, Lemma~A.8.1, printed p.~1733; Proposition~A.8.2, printed p.~1733). The normalized potential descends genuinely, is ambient H\"older of exponent $1/3$, has forced scalar $c=M/\nu(X)$, and solves the equation on every resolution and common refinement. The datum gives the cusp locus zero mass; near it the exact downstairs density is $\lambda f/\rho$, with $\rho=4|z|^2+9|z|^4$ (Book, Theorem~A.8.2, printed p.~1734). Separately, the existing bounded-mass theorem on the positive repaired normalization gives bounded existence for every nonzero nonnegative normalization-side $L^p$ density, $p>1$, without the smallness condition (Book, Corollary~A.8.1, printed p.~1736). Regularity and entire bounded-class uniqueness are established here for the small Sobolev regime. The original general problem remains open.\par Separately, the adapted-volume monomial criterion on a normal full-dimensional affine toric space with effective rational boundary and $\mathbb Q$-Cartier log canonical divisor identifies local and global holomorphic-character integrability with the interior of its shifted Newton set (Book, Theorem~A.4.1, printed p.~1710). The proof uses a strict recession inequality and translated-cone bounds on the actual logarithmic neighborhoods, rather than a simplicial quotient assumption. Subtracting any positive real multiple of a monomial ideal weight gives the simultaneous shifted tests (Book, Corollary~A.4.1, printed p.~1711). On the three-dimensional quadric $X=\{xw=yz\}$, with zero boundary and $u_\lambda=\lambda\log(|x|^2+|y|^2+|z|^2+|w|^2)$, the whole-germ adapted ideal at the vertex is $\mathfrak m_o^{\max\{0,\lfloor\lambda\rfloor-1\}}$ (Book, Proposition~A.4.3, printed p.~1711). Its constant germ is integrable exactly for $\lambda<2$. These are integral and ideal computations using the adapted canonical volume; they do not give existence or uniqueness for arbitrary singular-space Monge--Amp\`ere equations or replace resolution-ideal equivalence.
formal_entries.gap: Find assumptions giving finite mass, existence, uniqueness in the specified class, and continuity downstairs, stable under common refinements. Arbitrary unibranch singularities are not covered by log-terminal results. Scalar bounds and resolution-level regularity do not alone supply descent or control near the singular locus. Torus normalization, finitely many logarithmic poles and normalization-side integrability are fixed hypotheses. The curve theorem gives no criterion for arbitrary singularity types or higher-dimensional nonclosed backgrounds. A criterion for arbitrary integrable normalization-side data remains open. The explicit endpoint construction does not prove a mass or uniqueness theorem for the whole resolution-ideal class.
