formal_entries.label: qu:ot-bounded-mass
formal_entries.title: Mass bounds on Oeljeklaus--Toma manifolds
formal_entries.text: Does $X$ have the bounded mass property, that is, is $v_+(\omega)<+\infty$? Is $v_-(\omega)>0$? Equivalently, is $F(u)$ bounded above on smooth $\omega$-plurisubharmonic functions, and is $\inf_u(M_\omega(Au)+F(u))>0$? Ask also whether finite upper mass and positive lower mass hold on Oeljeklaus--Toma manifolds of any type $(s,t)$ with $s\geq2$.
formal_entries.state: Proposition~28.19.1, printed p.~1426 proves the exact identity $M_\omega(u)=M_\omega(Au)+F(u)$ for smooth potentials. For bounded potentials depending only on $y$, put $u=g(\log y_1,\log y_2)$, $P=1-\partial_1g$ and $Q=1-\partial_2g$. The function $g$ is Lipschitz; both $P$ and $Q$ have positive lower and finite upper bounds depending only on the unit lattice. Their product gives the normalized mass, so the masses in this invariant sector have uniform positive lower and finite upper bounds. Small transverse Fourier modes give masses on both sides of $\int_X\omega^3$. Proposition~28.19.2, printed p.~1429 excludes every Hermitian metric whose $\ddc$ has either sign on complex $2$-planes when the type is $(s,1)$ with $s\geq2$. Thus the usual sufficient curvature criteria in dimension three cannot decide this example. Metric independence of the two mass properties and the density of smooth strict potentials reduce the question to the displayed smooth fluctuation term.
formal_entries.gap: Control the fluctuations subject to the full positivity constraint $\omega+\ddc u\geq0$. The invariant estimates do not control arbitrary dependence on the fiber coordinates; absence of a metric with signed $\ddc$ proves neither infinite upper mass nor vanishing lower mass. Even the type $(2,1)$ case remains open.
formal_entries.source: Book, Section~28.19, especially the mass formula and the obstruction to metrics with signed $\ddc$; historical attribution in Section~34.16.

formal_entries.label: qu:foliated-rigidity
formal_entries.title: Continuity from Liouville null leaves
formal_entries.text: Is every function in $\PSH(X,\theta)$ continuous? If not, describe the possible singularity types in terms of the closures of the null leaves.
formal_entries.state: Theorem~28.19.1, printed p.~1423 answers this affirmatively for the natural transverse form on every Oeljeklaus--Toma manifold. On the universal cover every potential is $u(w,z)=f(y)+\sum_j\log y_j$, where $f$ is finite convex and obeys $f(\sigma(\varepsilon)y)=f(y)-\sum_j\log\sigma_j(\varepsilon)$. Liouville constancy removes the complex leaf coordinates; density of the real translations makes the potential independent of the real parts of $w$. Convexity then gives continuity. Corollary~28.19.1, printed p.~1424 gives a single ordinary singularity type, zero Lelong numbers, trivial multiplier ideals and zero top Monge--Amp\`ere measure in this class. On Inoue surfaces there nevertheless are currents supported on real torus hypersurfaces with continuous potentials. Thus continuity of a potential does not mean smoothness of its current.
formal_entries.gap: Replace the special real translation action by hypotheses on an arbitrary null foliation. Constancy on leaves by itself does not provide a transverse convex description or control values on exceptional leaf closures. Pullbacks from holomorphic fibrations can have singular potentials, but their fiber closures have real codimension $2r$ and hence do not satisfy the stated codimension hypothesis.
formal_entries.source: Book, Section~28.19 and the discussion preceding Problem~33.3.7; historical attribution in Section~34.16.

supplemental_entries.title: Support and pluripolarity of excess-mass defect measures
supplemental_entries.statement:
For the smooth admissible sequence in \bk{cor:smooth-capacity-mass-defect}, $w_j\to0$ in capacity, the masses equal a prescribed $b>\int_X\omega^n$, and a subsequence satisfies
\[(\omega+\ddc w_j)^n\rightharpoonup\omega^n+\sigma,\qquad
 \sigma(X)=b-\int_X\omega^n.\]
Determine which supports and pluripolar charging behaviors are possible for these defect measures.
supplemental_entries.state: The shallow truncation regions converge in total variation to $\omega^n$; every fixed deep-tail restriction has weak limit $\sigma$. The currents converge in coefficient $L^1$ and their Gauduchon traces in total variation. These strong linear convergences do not remove the nonlinear defect. A separate local example shows that smooth bounded psh functions on any bounded domain in $\mathbb C^n$, $n\geq2$, can tend to zero in every finite $L^p$ norm and in local capacity while their measures $(\ddc u_j)^n$ tend vaguely to $c\delta_a$, for any $c>0$ and interior point $a$ (Book, Proposition~1.6.3, printed p.~27; the point-mass case of \cite[v1, Corollary 3.6, p.~14]{QinLimits26}). A common local bound would force the limit measure at the zero potential to vanish, by Book, Lemma~1.6.6. This bounded-domain construction is distinct from the fixed global Hermitian-background sequence displayed in S01 and does not prescribe its defect measure. More generally, for every bounded psh background $b$ on such a domain and every positive Radon measure $\nu$, there are bounded $u_j\leq b$ tending to $b$ in all finite $L^p$ norms and in local capacity, with $(\ddc u_j)^n\to(\ddc b)^n+\nu$ vaguely (Book, Theorem~1.6.4, printed p.~32; \cite[v1, Theorem B, p.~3]{QinLimits26}). The measure may have infinite total mass. The book gives smooth approximants when $b$ is smooth and proves the addition by lower-degree trace control and finite atomic iteration; this still does not prescribe the fixed global defect in S01. At the zero background, every vaguely closed subset of the positive Radon measures is the full vague cluster set of a sequence of smooth bounded negative psh functions tending to zero in every finite $L^p$ norm and in local capacity, on a bounded domain in $\mathbb C^n$, $n\geq2$ (Book, Theorem~1.6.5, printed p.~35; the zero-potential case of \cite[v1, Theorem A, pp.~2--3]{QinLimits26}). The empty cluster set is allowed. A vague metric transfers corresponding subsequential limits without assuming that moving target measures have uniformly bounded local masses; it does not imply convergence of their difference on every continuous compactly supported test (Book, Lemma~1.6.12 and the following counterexample, printed pp.~32--35). For a fixed bounded psh background $b$, the full vague cluster sets of bounded approximants $u_j\leq b$ tending to $b$ in all finite $L^p$ norms and in local capacity are exactly the vaguely closed sets all of whose members dominate $(\ddc b)^n$ (Book, Lemma~1.6.13 and Theorem~1.6.6, printed pp.~36--37). The empty set remains allowed, and the book gives smooth approximants for smooth $b$. The measure lower bound uses the capacity convergence in this regime; it is distinct from the source's general $L^1$ reachable-set classification. This full-cluster-set conclusion is local and leaves the fixed global S01 defect question open.\par The global smooth shrinking construction now has additional necessary restrictions (Book, Proposition~7.5.1, printed p.~277). For $H_j=\ddc w_j+s_j\omega\geq0$, every subsequential limit $K_k$ of $H_j^k$ is positive and closed, pairs to zero with every smooth complementary $\mathrm d$-closed or $\ddc$-closed form, and satisfies $K_1=K_n=0$. The defect is $\sum_{k=2}^{n-1}\binom nk\omega^{n-k}\wedge K_k$. A global closed semipositive form confines its support to that form's degeneracy set. There is no such excess in dimensions at most two, or on a threefold carrying a pluriclosed Hermitian metric. This statement uses global test forms and does not infer a restriction from a merely local K\"ahler form.\par On the standard Hopf threefold $X=(\mathbb C^3\setminus\{0\})/\langle z\mapsto\mathrm e^{-1}z\rangle$, Book, Theorem~8.9.1, printed p.~313 gives a complete classification: for $b>6$, all defects are $\mathcal L\mu$, the Haar-probability fiber lifts of arbitrary positive measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb P^2$ of mass $b-6$. Every one is realized by normalized smooth $w_j=r_jU_j$ with exact mass $b$ and $0<r_j<\varepsilon_j$ for any prescribed bounds $\varepsilon_j\to0$. Their supports are precisely saturated supports $\pi^{-1}(\operatorname{supp}\mu)$, with every nonempty closed saturated set realizable; they have no point atoms. They charge no pluripolar sets exactly when $\mu$ charges no base pluripolar sets. Smooth full-support defects, a full defect supported on one globally pluripolar fiber, and full-support defects assigning any fraction strictly between zero and one to a polar fiber all occur. The positive quadratic estimate (Book, Lemma~8.9.1, printed p.~309), orbital mixture construction for every probability law, including singular laws (Book, Proposition~8.9.1, printed p.~309), full intermediate-tensor necessity (Book, Lemma~8.9.2, printed p.~311), and repaired projective automorphisms (Book, Lemma~8.9.3, printed p.~312) prove full continuous-test convergence while retaining positivity and exact total mass.\par For every Hermitian metric $\Omega$ on this same Hopf threefold, Book, Theorem~8.9.2, printed p.~314 classifies the defects as $\mathcal L_\Omega\mu$ with mass $\mu(\mathbb P^2)=b-\int_X\Omega^3$. The fiber probability is $\Omega|_{\pi^{-1}(p)}/\int_{\pi^{-1}(p)}\Omega$, which need not be Haar. Supports, absence of point atoms, and the pluripolar equivalence are unchanged. The prescribed-mass correction solves the actual quadratic mass polynomial, including its linear term. Thus the entire metric family is settled, while general manifolds remain outside this classification.
supplemental_entries.gap: Determine sufficient realization conditions on a general compact Hermitian manifold for positive closed intermediate currents with the stated vanishing pairings, and classify the resulting supports and pluripolar charging behaviors. The displayed shrinking smooth construction on the standard Hopf threefold is completely classified for every Hermitian metric, but the necessary current restrictions alone do not prove sufficiency on other manifolds.

supplemental_entries.title: Optimal damping on the Hopf BMP counterexample
supplemental_entries.statement: For the standard Hermitian Hopf threefold, determine the optimal decay conditions on a decreasing weight $W(t)$ ensuring finite weighted measures $W(-u)\mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_\omega(u)$ for all normalized $u\leq0$, with uniform tail and capacity-continuity bounds.
supplemental_entries.state:
BMP fails on this threefold, while $v_-(\omega)=6$. The general damping theorem gives these conclusions for
\[W(t)=(1+t)^{-1}[\log(\mathrm e+t)]^{-a},\qquad a>1.\]
Exponential damping and stronger decay are available. The upper-mass counterexample is from Xia--Zhang \cite{XZ26}.\par For positive $C^1$ nonincreasing weights tending to zero, the entire normalized class invariant under $(z_0,z')\mapsto(z_0,Az')$, $A\in U(2)$, has sharp thresholds (Book, Theorem~8.8.3, printed p.~306). Every individual weighted measure is finite if and only if $\sup_{t\gg1}\sqrt t\,W(t)<+\infty$, which is also equivalent to uniform total-mass bounds. Uniform deep tails, uniform capacity absolute continuity and capacity-to-weak continuity instead hold if and only if $\sqrt t\,W(t)\to0$. These assertions cover bounded and unbounded potentials in that full invariant class. The uniform estimates are $12Q(W)$ and $12Q_T(W)$, where $Q_T(W)=\sup_{t\geq T}(1+\sqrt{2t})W(t)$. For $W(t)=(1+t)^{-p}[\log(\mathrm e+t)]^{-a}$, modified smoothly on a compact interval, finiteness and uniform masses hold exactly for $p>1/2$ or $p=1/2,a\geq0$; the stronger properties require $p>1/2$ or $p=1/2,a>0$ (Book, Corollary~8.8.2, printed p.~307).\par The heat construction gives the necessary square-root conditions even for the unrestricted class (Book, Corollary~8.8.1, printed p.~302), and a single genuine normalized potential with infinite weighted measure whenever $\sqrt t\,W(t)$ is unbounded (Book, Theorem~8.8.2, printed p.~303). When the square-root quantity is bounded but does not tend to zero, smooth invariant potentials converge in capacity to a logarithmic divisor potential while a weak cluster measure charges its pole divisor (Book, Lemma~8.8.4, printed p.~306). The non-pluripolar weighted measure of the limit gives that divisor zero mass. The sufficiency proof uses symmetry and does not solve the unrestricted problem.
supplemental_entries.gap: Determine optimal necessary and sufficient decay conditions for all normalized potentials on the standard Hopf threefold. The square-root scale is necessary, whereas the unrestricted sufficient condition remains $\int_0^{+\infty}(1+t)(-W'(t))\,\mathrm dt<+\infty$. The rotational class is completely treated, with separate finiteness and continuity thresholds; no reduction of arbitrary angular data to that class is established.

supplemental_entries.title: Exponential solvability when the individual threshold is zero
supplemental_entries.statement:
Let $v_-(h)=0$, let $f\geq0$ be a nonzero $L^1$ density with $b_h(f)=0$, and fix $\lambda>0$. Characterize when a genuine $s\in\PSH(X,h)$ satisfies
\[\mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_h(s)\geq\mathrm e^{\lambda s}f\,\mathrm dV,\]
and hence when the greatest finite-mass exponential solution exists. In particular, test the obstructing concentration density constructed in the lower-mass chapter.
supplemental_entries.state: Positive threshold supplies an exponential subsolution for every exponent. Any exponential subsolution gives a greatest exact solution by decreasing bounded-density approximation. The concentration argument excludes all positive scaled subsolutions and therefore all bounded exponential solutions. On a split product $X_0\times\mathbf P^k$, $k\geq1$, with $m=\dim X_0$, $H=h_0+\kappa$ and normalized Fubini--Study form $\kappa$, put $C=\binom{m+k}{m}$, $V_0=\int_{X_0}h_0^m$ and $R=(V_0^{-1}h_0^m\wedge\kappa^k)/\mathrm dV$. For $\psi=\log(\sum_{i=1}^k|Z_i|^2/\sum_{i=0}^k|Z_i|^2)$ and the canonical projective pole $u_\alpha=1-(1-\psi)^\alpha$, $0<\alpha<1$, write $\mathrm{MA}_\kappa(u_\alpha)=q_\alpha\kappa^k$. Book, Lemma~14.34.1, printed p.~685 gives the radial weighted growth. Theorem~14.34.2, printed p.~686 proves the sufficient condition $f/R\leq A_\lambda q_\alpha\mathrm e^{-\lambda u_\alpha}$ with finite $A_\lambda$: the genuine barrier $u_\alpha+\lambda^{-1}\log(CV_0/A_\lambda)$ has actual mass $CV_0$, and a uniform subexponential growth condition in $(1-\psi)^\alpha$ supplies this bound for every $\lambda>0$. Theorem~14.34.3, printed p.~687 tailors smooth positive projective components to every prescribed smooth collapsing base sequence. Their weighted sum is one finite, strictly positive $L^1$ probability density with $b_H(f)=0$, independent of $\lambda$, admitting greatest genuine unbounded exact solutions of finite positive mass for every positive exponent. The elliptic threefold yields fourfold and fivefold examples; $96\pi$ and $240\pi$ are masses of the explicit subsolutions, not of the exact solutions. Proposition~14.34.2, printed p.~689 shows that the admitted positive exponents form an upper interval, with a positive lower endpoint possibly included or excluded. Proposition~14.34.3, printed p.~689 proves that, whenever genuine exact solutions exist along exponents $\lambda_j\downarrow0$ for a fixed zero-threshold density, their scalars $c_j=\mathrm e^{\lambda_j\sup_Xu_j}$ and total masses tend to zero. Also $\lambda_j\sup_Xu_j\to-\infty$, and $\mathrm e^{\lambda_ju_j}\to0$ uniformly. This applies to any choice of exact solutions for the tailored density; normalized-potential convergence is not inferred. Lemma~14.34.2, printed p.~690 gives a common continuous upper barrier for all genuine exponential subsolutions with exponents bounded away from zero, and a logarithmically corrected order for greatest solutions. Proposition~14.34.4, printed p.~691 shows that a positive infimum of the nonempty solvable interval is admitted exactly when some genuine exact solution sequence approaching it from above has uniformly bounded-below suprema. At an excluded positive endpoint, every exact solution sequence has uniform exponential collapse and total mass tending to zero. Proposition~14.34.5, printed p.~692 gives right $L^1$ and capacity continuity of greatest solutions at every admitted positive exponent, with total-variation convergence of the equation measures. Proposition~14.34.6, printed p.~692 gives an exact left limit below the greatest solution at every positive exponent in the interior of the solvable interval, with $L^1$ and capacity convergence of the potentials and total-variation convergence of their equation measures. Proposition~14.34.7, printed p.~693 shows that exponents where this left limit differs from the greatest solution form an at most countable set; elsewhere the greatest family is two-sided continuous in those topologies. General S03 remains open.
supplemental_entries.gap: Find a necessary and sufficient intrinsic criterion at $b_h(f)=0$, and decide solvability for arbitrary previously prescribed concentration-family choices. The reviewed theorem chooses the projective components after the collapsing base sequence; it does not classify all choices, establish necessity of the radial bound or construct a nonsolvable zero-threshold exponential example. This remains distinct from P07, which assumes a positive individual threshold. Determine the lower endpoint by intrinsic conditions on the density, and establish whether excluded positive endpoints can occur or whether the at most countable jump set must be empty.

supplemental_entries.title: Order-continuity of the density-root space at zero lower mass
supplemental_entries.statement: Write $\rho_h(p)=b_h(|p|^n)^{-1/n}$, $\mathcal D_h=\{p\in L^n:\rho_h(p)<\infty\}$, and let $\mathcal D_h^0$ be the closure of bounded roots in $\|p\|_{L^n}+\rho_h(p)$. If $v_-(h)=0$, is $\mathcal D_h^0=\mathcal D_h$? Separately, do uniform root tails suffice for the exact equation in P07?
supplemental_entries.state:
The manuscript proves
\[p\in\mathcal D_h^0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \rho_h(|p|\mathbf1_{\{|p|>K\}})\to0.\]
This is equivalent to norm convergence under all dominated perturbations tending to zero in measure. Smooth functions are dense in $\mathcal D_h^0$, which contains $L^r$ for $r>n$. If lower mass is positive, both spaces equal $L^n$. Root tails give scalar continuity, dual attainment and error moduli for exponential approximations. Proposition~14.31.5, printed p.~674 identifies the closed subspace $J(L^N(Y,\kappa^k))\subset\mathcal D_H^0$, where $J\xi=R^{1/N}\pi_Y^*\xi$, with $\|J\xi\|_{L^N}=\|\xi\|_{L^N}$ and $\rho_H(J\xi)=c_0^{-1/N}\|\xi\|_{L^N}$. This uses all Gauduchon tests on the product. Its uniform tails vanish for every factor root. In the projective radial family, some such roots lie in no $L^r$ with $r>N$, and their root tails are comparable to $(\log K)^{-k(1-\alpha)/N}$. For $n\geq3$, Theorem~14.32.1, printed p.~675 gives a sufficient condition on a fixed datum: if $\int_Ef\,\mathrm dV\leq A\operatorname{Cap}_h(E)^{1+\alpha}$ for all Borel $E$, with $A,\alpha>0$, then $0<b_h(f)<\infty$, $f^{1/n}\in\mathcal D_h^0$, and normalized clipped solutions have a uniformly convergent subsequence solving $\mathrm{MA}_h(\phi)=b_h(f)f\,\mathrm dV$ with $\phi$ continuous. For every $0\leq g\leq f$ of positive integral, $b_h(g)\geq C(\int_Xg\,\mathrm dV)^{-\alpha/(1+\alpha)}$ and $\rho_h(g^{1/n})\leq C'(\int_Xg\,\mathrm dV)^{\alpha/(n(1+\alpha))}$. Theorem~14.32.2, printed p.~677 constructs such a logarithmic density on each fixed Hermitian background, including one of zero lower mass, with $b_h(f)=1$, no $L^p$ integrability for any $p>1$, and $\rho_h(f^{1/n}\mathbf1_{\{f>K\}})\leq C(\log K)^{-\alpha}$. The capacity bound is an additional hypothesis; neither general S04 question nor general P07 is settled. No homogeneous potential uniqueness or selection of the greatest exponential family is inferred.
supplemental_entries.gap: Determine whether positive-threshold roots can have nonvanishing uniform tails. Even equality of the spaces would not automatically prove capacity convergence of equation potentials; that further implication needs a compactness argument.

supplemental_entries.title: Canonical selection and whole-family convergence at exponent zero
supplemental_entries.statement: For greatest positive-exponent solutions with fixed density and prescribed reference, determine conditions under which the normalized potentials converge to one canonical zero-exponent solution as $\lambda\downarrow0$. Extend the question to varying model references and densities while retaining their limiting type.
supplemental_entries.state: Under suitable lower-mass or model-volume hypotheses, scalars and equation measures converge; each normalized cluster limit solves the zero-exponent equation. Smooth and specified semipositive dual maximizers give uniqueness and whole-family convergence. The symmetric projective example has an explicitly selected limit. General Hermitian zero-exponent potentials need not be unique: smooth, quadratic-zero and real-analytic-density counterexamples are constructed. Theorem~14.35.1, printed p.~696 determines the entire supremum-normalized greatest family for the explicit sublogarithmic $L^1$ densities on zero-lower-mass Hermitian products, with $L^1$, capacity and local uniform convergence off the pole fiber. The density parameter and exponent may vary at independent rates; the reference remains zero. Proposition~14.35.1, printed p.~697 gives the moment boundary $\alpha=k/(k+1)$: below it the scalar-centered family converges to $u_\alpha-M_\alpha$, while at and above it the centering error tends to $+\infty$ even though the scalars tend to the positive threshold. Corollary~14.35.1, printed p.~699 characterizes the selected critical potential in the separated class. These results concern the radial family. Theorem~15.13.1, printed p.~759 gives whole-family selection for logarithmic ordinary models with a positive residual on $\mathbb P^1$ times any compact Hermitian factor. Reference coefficients, positive background functions, continuous positive factor densities and exponent may vary at independent rates. Normalized and scalar-centered potentials converge in $L^1$, capacity and locally uniformly off the fixed divisor; the equation measures converge in total variation. The scalar error uses each parameter's own critical constant. Proposition~15.13.1, printed p.~757 computes the ordinary models and their continuous residuals, while Lemma~15.13.1, printed p.~758 gives greatestness on the entire one-sided ordinary class. Corollary~15.13.1, printed p.~762 proves maximality of the critical coefficient on that class and uniqueness and mean order in its separated sector. General singular-reference selection and nonseparated critical uniqueness remain open.
supplemental_entries.gap: A general selection requires more than uniqueness of the scalar. Prove uniqueness of the selected limit or provide a robust variational or order characterization, particularly for $L^1$ data. Separate selection from the disproved assertion that all normalized solutions are unique. Related targets are P07 and S16.

supplemental_entries.title: Regularity for arbitrary prescribed types and at density zeros
supplemental_entries.statement: Find regularity and stability criteria for solutions in arbitrary prescribed ordinary or envelope types on a smooth big, possibly nonclosed background, beyond the resolved logarithmic and exceptional minimal types. At a density zero, identify conditions on the density and residual geometry that imply a smooth or H\"older residual, and state whether the conclusion extends across the singular set. Also obtain regularity criteria for general singular envelopes and weighted extremals beyond the stated density-in-capacity regimes.
supplemental_entries.state: The manuscript gives local continuity above a locally bounded strict barrier, local H\"older control for minimal $L^p$ solutions, and interior smoothness on the full regular locus of a fixed analytic strict barrier with smooth positive density. Resolved logarithmic types with positive residual and exceptional blowups have quantified H\"older remainders. Smooth positive global volume forms give ample-locus smoothness in every closed big K\"ahler class. On a smaller smooth-density open set there are compact examples of discontinuous bounded solutions. Smooth density zeros and their necessary vanishing order do not suffice for a smooth Hessian. Weighted extremals have regularity in specified uniform density-in-capacity regimes, which do not cover every singular envelope. Theorem~15.14.1, printed p.~769 proves a relative-density criterion in each prescribed radial nonlogarithmic type on projective space: an $O(r^\delta)$ relative error gives a H\"older residual, a $C^1$ residual at $\delta\ge1/2$, and a $C^2$ residual at $\delta\ge1$, without differentiating the density error. The canonical pole remains. Proposition~15.14.1, printed p.~771 gives smoothly flat residuals from flat errors, while Proposition~15.14.2, printed p.~772 proves the sharp derivative and H\"older thresholds by compact mass-preserving examples. Proposition~15.14.3, printed p.~772 constructs a globally smooth residual despite an open density-zero annulus. Corollary~15.14.1, printed p.~773 transfers these results to a nonclosed zero-lower-mass product under the stated factor hypothesis.\par Book, Theorem~15.15.1, printed p.~775 identifies the full everywhere obstacle envelope for $u_\alpha+F(\log r)$ on $\mathbb P^k$, $k\ge2$, $0<\alpha<1$, $F\in C_c^2(\mathbb R)$. Its convex-minorant formula retains the ordinary sublogarithmic type and gives a globally $C^{1,1}$ residual, zero near the pole and smooth near infinity. Book, Corollary~15.15.1, printed p.~776 gives its actual unit non-pluripolar mass, zero measure on free intervals and uniform value contraction. Book, Theorem~15.15.2, printed p.~777 proves uniform global $C^{1,1}$ residual bounds for a fixed support interval and bounded $\|F\|_\infty+\|F''\|_\infty$, together with $C^{1,\gamma}$ stability of order $\|F-G\|_\infty^{(1-\gamma)/2}$ for $0<\gamma<1$. The projective-end estimates remain uniform through moving infinity contact; no common right cutoff is assumed. Book, Proposition~15.15.1, printed p.~778 identifies the full envelope on a product with any fixed compact positive Hermitian $m$-fold, gives the measure $\binom{k+m}{k}\operatorname{MA}_\kappa(E_F)\otimes h_0^m$, and proves ordinary stretching-class membership and the same residual estimates. Book, Example~15.15.1, printed p.~779 supplies a nonclosed non-K\"ahler fourfold using a Hopf surface factor. No mass property of the factor is required.
supplemental_entries.gap: Find sufficient type-sensitive hypotheses covering the remaining cases. Local density smoothness alone and determinant vanishing order alone are already insufficient. Regularity across the pole set must be justified separately from regularity on its complement. The radial criterion relies on positive cumulative central mass and an exact radial inverse. It does not settle nonsymmetric data, arbitrary singular reference types or general weighted extremals. The singular-obstacle criterion requires the everywhere radial obstacle and fixed-support $C^2$ bounds for uniform estimates. General compact obstacle sets, ideal weighted envelopes and arbitrary prescribed reference types remain open; the derivative stability does not assert $C^{1,1}$ convergence.

supplemental_entries.title: Weak adjoints for singular references and a weak linearized equation
supplemental_entries.statement:
In every admissible singular-reference or degenerate-background regime of the normalization functional, determine when $\mathcal A_\varphi(F)$ is a singleton and when its probability is an approximation-independent adjoint of a weak linearized Monge--Amp\`ere operator. Specify a meaningful product and weight for
\[\ddc\bigl(\rho(\theta+\ddc u)^{n-1}\bigr)=0.\]
supplemental_entries.state:
Supporting probabilities and their stability are constructed without declaring this product defined. Generic uniqueness holds on a dense $G_\delta$ for each fixed admissible reference. Smooth potentials have the classical adjoint. If every smooth positive potential perturbation is Gauduchon, normalized Monge--Amp\`ere measures extend bounded adjoints and are continuous under bounded capacity convergence; this includes Gauduchon surfaces.
 Lemma 15.2.1, printed p.~712, gives an admissible ordinary divisorial model on $\mathbb P^1	imes\mathbb P^1$. With normalized pulled Fubini--Study forms, $	heta=2\omega_1+2\omega_2$, $ eta=\omega_1+2\omega_2$, $\mathrm dV=\omega_1\wedge\omega_2$ and $\psi=\log(|z|^2/(1+|z|^2))$, Proposition 15.2.4, printed p.~712, proves that every bounded-equivalent representative has non-pluripolar mass four, the sole support at $F=0$ is $\mathrm dV$, and the residual adjoint cofactor is $ eta/4$. Theorem 15.2.5, printed p.~714, constructs monotone uniformly positive smoothings $u_{\delta,g}=\log(r+\delta\mathrm e^g)$, where $r=|z|^2/(1+|z|^2)$ and $g$ is smooth on the second factor with $\ddc g\geq-\omega_2$. They converge canonically, in capacity and smoothly off $D=\{0\}	imes\mathbb P^1$, with $F_{\delta,g}=\log((	heta+\ddc u_{\delta,g})^2/(4\mathrm dV))	o0$ in every finite $L^p$. Yet their classical adjoint probabilities tend to $	frac12\mathrm dV+	frac12[D]\wedge\omega_2+	frac18[D]\wedge\ddc g$, which depends on $g$ and has divisor mass one half. Smooth mass eight differs from relative mass four, and the exponential densities fail uniform integrability. Section 34.11, printed p.~1674, explains the exact bounded-product, extension and integration premises.
 Corollary 15.2.1, printed p.~716, proves recovery in this fixed divisor type when $w_j,w\in\operatorname{PSH}(X, eta)$ have one common bound $|w_j|,|w|\leq M$ and $w_j	o w$ in capacity. The residual cofactors $Q_j=( eta+\ddc w_j)/4$ converge as currents and the residual probabilities $
u_j=( eta+\ddc w_j)^2/4$ converge weakly. The estimate in equation 15.9, printed p.~716, gives the quantitative bound $|\int f(\mathrm d
u_j-\mathrm d
u)|\leq C_f(2\eta+2M^2\operatorname{Cap}_ eta\{|w_j-w|>\eta\})$ when $-C_f eta\leq\ddc f\leq C_f eta$. When the residual forms are smooth and strictly positive these are their classical adjoints; the canonical singular potentials retain the same divisor. At a continuous relative solution the limiting probability is the sole supporting probability. Theorem~15.13.2, printed p.~764 identifies the full supporting set on $C(X)$ for a non-Gauduchon logarithmic product surface with continuous positive residual form. The weak linearization has a unique invariant Borel probability, equal to the supporting probability; its normalized measurable adjoint weight is unique. Lemma~15.13.2, printed p.~763 supplies the signed-measure uniqueness argument without a density regularity premise. Proposition~15.13.2, printed p.~765 proves approximation independence of probabilities, weighted currents and weight measures for a fixed divisor and uniformly convergent positive residual forms, including approximations depending on both variables. Example~15.13.1, printed p.~766 gives a Lipschitz nonsmooth datum and a pole-filling family whose classical adjoints retain divisor mass.
supplemental_entries.gap: Unrestricted smooth recovery fails even for this admissible reference with singleton support and a defined residual adjoint. The fixed divisor and uniformly bounded residual capacity-convergence regime is established above. Recovery for more general singular references or unbounded residual sequences, and recovery of varying conformal multipliers without uniform positive-residual-form convergence, remain open, as does the construction of an approximation-independent weak operator in the general singular-reference or degenerate-background regime. The positive result is conditional on the stated residual approximation; it does not assert that every bounded residual has such a smooth approximation. P16 asks the narrower singleton question for a Hermitian background and nonsingular reference; neither this concentration example nor this fixed-divisor result resolves it. The new non-Gauduchon result controls varying conformal weights only under fixed-divisor, uniform positive-residual-form convergence. It does not establish recovery under potential convergence alone, uniqueness for arbitrary continuous singular equations, or a weak adjoint for general singular residual products.

supplemental_entries.title: Continuity when singular references or positive residuals degenerate
supplemental_entries.statement: Give geometric or singularity conditions on varying admissible references $\varphi_j$ and backgrounds that imply convergence of $B_{\varphi_j}$ on continuous tests and place all cluster supports in $\mathcal A_\varphi(F)$ for the limiting reference. Include degenerate residual forms and arbitrary singularities.
supplemental_entries.state: A genuine smaller-background envelope tending to reference zero gives uniform convergence of scalar functionals and uniformly integrable supports. Relative comparison of positive divisorial residuals gives a geometric criterion. Entropy estimates yield compactness while references vary. BMP model-volume and fixed-divisor regimes supply additional equation stability. For closed projective backgrounds and one fixed point blowup, Theorem~15.11.1, printed p.~743, proves uniform convergence on all continuous tests from Hausdorff convergence of convex bodies containing one common translated simplex and positive scales tending to a positive limit. The actual limiting ordinary model has positive mass and is independently solvable for every bounded Borel test; supporting probabilities are the normalized exponential densities. Proposition~15.11.1, printed p.~744, and Corollary~15.11.1, printed p.~745, give a varying nonanalytic isolated-pole family with positive limiting mass. Proposition~15.11.2, printed p.~747, and Corollary~15.11.2, printed p.~747, give smooth residuals that have rank one on an exceptional divisor but positive top mass; the zero-mass endpoint is excluded for every bounded ordinary-type remainder.
supplemental_entries.gap: The common-simplex criterion settles these closed projective and fixed-blowup families, including the two stated degenerations. Extend it to nonclosed Hermitian backgrounds, moving modifications or unrestricted singularity degeneration. Compactness of measures alone does not identify their supporting functional; limiting-reference solvability must be established. These results do not assert convergence of solution potentials or define rough weighted adjoint products.

supplemental_entries.title: Zero-obstacle equality versus equality at every obstacle
supplemental_entries.statement:
For an admissible smooth background $\theta$ and $u\in\PSH(X,\theta)$, does
\[P_\theta[u]=P_\theta[u]_{\mathcal I}\]
imply $P_{\theta,F}[u]=P_{\theta,F}[u]_{\mathcal I}$ for every smooth real obstacle $F$, without positive lower ideal volume or BMP?
supplemental_entries.state: All-obstacle equality always implies zero-obstacle equality. The converse follows from membership in the relative envelope class of the ideal envelope. Under BMP and positive lower ideal volume it is a theorem; on curves it holds without volume restrictions. It also holds on specified separated products, auxiliary products without ambient BMP, and divisorial curve fibrations with the stated descent hypotheses. All-obstacle uniformity is smooth-gauge invariant. Book, Theorem~16.6.3, printed p.~807 constructs nonpositive potentials with poles on any prescribed countable set, including a dense set, on every positive Hermitian background. One fixed stronger potential supplies all finite stretching competitors; exponential integrability at every positive scale makes all multiplier ideals trivial. Book, Proposition~16.6.8, printed p.~809 proves that both envelopes equal the unrestricted envelope below every continuous obstacle, using the book's ideal-equivalence definition. This is an explicit sufficient family; no mass or volume assertion and no general S09 implication is inferred.
supplemental_entries.gap: Establish the converse in unrestricted higher-dimensional zero-volume and unbounded-mass settings or give a counterexample. The positive-volume criterion cannot be applied at lower volume zero. This is an explicit subproblem overlapping P06 and the analytic-closure part of P01/P17.

supplemental_entries.title: Perron interpolation and a metric geometry of singularity classes
supplemental_entries.statement: Relate Hermitian Perron segments and their Legendre-dual test curves to geodesics for a complete metric on singularity classes. Identify hypotheses under which this interpolation is stationary for a specified action and compatible with a complete singularity topology.
supplemental_entries.state: The minimum principle and Legendre duality give Perron interpolation without a closed background. The raw $L^2$ Euler equation has torsion terms, and on a Gauduchon three-torus a smooth Perron segment need not be stationary. A primitive for the raw Monge--Amp\`ere one-form near zero forces closedness. On surfaces the Gauduchon condition persists but does not remove first-derivative torsion terms. There is now a complete restricted example on each nonproduct diagonal Hopf manifold $H_n$, $n\geq3$, with background $\omega_n=\pi^*\kappa+\beta_n$ and $\int\kappa^{n-1}=1$. Proposition~17.5.1, printed p.~902 proves that the full Hermitian Perron envelope between basic endpoints descends to the projective base; competitors need not be basic. It also proves the actual extended-measure identity $\operatorname{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{\omega_n}(\pi^*v)=n\beta_n\wedge\pi^*\operatorname{MA}_\kappa(v)$, with fiber factor two. Theorem~17.5.1, printed p.~903 gives the classical K\"ahler $L^2$ completion on canonical basic full-mass squared-energy potentials, with distance scaling $2\pi\sqrt{2n}$ from the base operator $\mathrm i\partial\bar\partial$. Its unique geodesic is the full Perron segment and attains the endpoints in $L^1$. Proposition~17.5.2, printed p.~904 proves metric-action minimization and raw-action agreement on smooth basic paths; a smooth basic Perron path is stationary under all smooth fixed-endpoint variations. Nevertheless Theorem~17.6.1, printed p.~906 gives infinitely many negative raw-action directions at each nonzero constant translation and strictly shorter nonbasic positive paths. The explicit threefold perturbation has action $3-3\pi^2\varepsilon^2/2+111\pi^4\varepsilon^4/64<3$ at $\varepsilon=1/100$. Proposition~17.7.1, printed p.~907 computes nonconstant diagonal geodesics and their exact distances. Proposition~17.7.2, printed p.~908 gives actual full-mass singular potentials $v_a=1-(1-\psi)^a$, where $\psi=\log(\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|z_j|^2/\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}|z_j|^2)$: squared energy is finite exactly for $a<(n-1)/(n+1)$, with logarithmic divergence at equality. Different exponents below this threshold give distinct ordinary types at finite positive basic distance. Proposition~17.8.1, printed p.~909 proves ordinary-envelope and Legendre pullback; every basic finite-energy point has ordinary model projection zero. The exact Darvas1401.7318v3 completion, endpoint, full-mass and bounded Dirichlet results remain classical closed-base inputs, explicitly identified in Chapter34.
supplemental_entries.gap: Construct a separating complete metric on general ordinary models, with compatibility under modifications and changes of background, and identify an action matching their Perron interpolation. The Hopf metric acts on potentials and does not separate ordinary model projections, which are all zero in its finite-energy domain. Its basic mass formula does not compute ordinary-type lower or upper volumes, which allow nonbasic competitors. Full raw-action minimization already fails at constant Hopf translations; no definiteness or completeness of the unrestricted raw-length infimum is claimed. General S10 remains open and connects P01/P17.

supplemental_entries.title: Nonclosed restricted positivity and its relation to intrinsic traces
supplemental_entries.statement: Construct a restricted positivity invariant for general nonclosed backgrounds and relate it to intrinsic multiplier-ideal trace data. Determine when positive residual or restricted mass produces a strict current of a specified one-sided or ordinary singularity type.
supplemental_entries.state: For closed classes on class-$\mathcal C$ manifolds, a finite resolution-independent restricted invariant is positive exactly when the resolved class is big; for nef classes its zero union is the null locus. For divisorial traces with bounded remainder, a mass polynomial and residual comparison produce strict currents more singular than the trace. The nonclosed ruled family $Y=\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$, $\theta=cw_1+aw_2$, $r=bG_p+1-(1-G_p)^\alpha$, with $c>0$, $b\geq0$, $0<\alpha<1$ and smooth $a>0$ on the first factor, goes beyond bounded residuals. Here $w$ is the probability Fubini--Study form and $\ddc G_p=[p]-w$. Its ordinary type is admissible exactly when $b<c$, and all rough representatives have finite positive mass. Theorem~19.10.1, printed p.~950 computes the two ordinary-type volumes as $2(c-b)\min a$ and $2(c-b)\max a$, including residual references with infinite first moment. Proposition~19.10.1, printed p.~952 gives ambient restricted ideals $\mathcal O_Y(-\lfloor sb\rfloor D)$ and intrinsic orders $b\operatorname{ord}_E(\pi^*D)$, with $D=\{p\}\times\mathbb P^1$, on every modification; the residual remains unbounded and nonanalytic. Both volumes survive pure pullback. Every nonempty finite composition of point blowups, including centers on $D$ or earlier exceptional curves, preserves positive lower volume but excludes a strict current in the pulled-back ordinary type, while permitting a one-sided strict representative (Proposition~19.10.3, printed p.~953). For a smooth first-factor probability density $m$, the separate residual Gauduchon volume is $2(c-b)/\int(m/a)w$, with an explicit all-test minimizer and subtraction cost (Proposition~26.21.3, printed p.~1225; Corollary~26.21.1, printed p.~1226).\par For a global quasi-plurisubharmonic residual $q$ whose ordinary type has representatives $q_\delta\sim q$ with $\ddc q_\delta\geq-\delta h$ for every $\delta>0$, Lemma~16.7.1, printed p.~891 proves zero point Lelong numbers and zero polar curvature on every smooth compact modification. Theorem~16.7.1, printed p.~892 characterizes strict currents in the ordinary type of $\sigma_\Delta+q$, for a finite effective real divisor $\Delta$: they exist exactly when $\theta-\chi_\Delta$ has a smooth strictly positive representative. The residual does not change ambient multiplier ideals at any real weight (Lemma~1.16.4, printed p.~71). If $\Delta$ has simple normal crossings and $Y$ is contained in none of its positive components, Proposition~19.2.2, printed p.~923 gives $\tau_{Y,\sigma_\Delta+q}(E)=\sum_j a_j\operatorname{ord}_E\rho^*(D_j|_Y)$ on every smooth compact modification $\rho:Z\to Y$, even when $q|_Y\equiv-\infty$. The small-curvature condition requires actual representatives of the same ordinary type; mere zero Lelong numbers are not substituted for it.
supplemental_entries.gap: Construct a restricted invariant for arbitrary nonclosed backgrounds beyond this ruled family and establish the precise relation to ambient intrinsic ideal data. A strictness criterion must distinguish one-sided domination from preservation of ordinary type and account for the blowup obstruction. Universal equality of restricted mass and ambient positive-product data is contradicted by the trace examples. General S11 remains open; this connects P06, P18 and P14.

supplemental_entries.title: Inverse realization of divisors at a global or prescribed-type threshold
supplemental_entries.statement: Given an effective real divisor $E$ and the annihilating face of normalized Gauduchon tests associated to its Bott--Chern class, determine when a threshold subsolution for $f$ has $\omega+\ddc u\geq[E]$. Separately formulate and characterize the maximal coefficient among potentials in one prescribed singularity type.
supplemental_entries.state:
If a coefficient-$c$ subsolution contains $[E]$, the manuscript proves
\[c\leq b_\omega(f)(1-\kappa_\omega(\beta_E))^n,\]
where $\beta_E$ represents $\{E\}$ and $\kappa_\omega$ is its linear positivity threshold. At $c=b_\omega(f)$, every smooth maximizing sequence annihilates $\beta_E$ in the limit; uniform integrability ensures its cluster current maximizes the dual functional. The corresponding exposed face lies in the weak closure of smooth tests. Lemma~15.9.1, printed p.~734 identifies the full one-sided divisorial class with all genuine potentials in the positive residual Hermitian background, preserving extended measures even with additional poles or infinite mass. Its ordinary envelope is of the prescribed type and meets the smaller-background model condition. Theorem~15.9.3, printed p.~735 identifies and attains the one-sided coefficient $b_{h-\beta_E}(f)$ for every nonzero nonnegative $L^1$ density. For smooth strictly positive data, the ordinary and relative envelope classes have the same attained finite-equation coefficient; it is strictly below the global coefficient whenever $E\ne0$. Corollary~15.9.1, printed p.~736 excludes nonzero divisorial components at a smooth positive global threshold. Example~15.9.1, printed p.~737 computes the prescribed/global coefficient ratio $(1-\lambda)^k$ on an explicit Fubini--Study product. Its nonclosed zero-lower-mass specialization retains the stated factor hypothesis.
supplemental_entries.gap: Determine sufficient conditions converting annihilation into an actual divisorial component. Do not assume all Gauduchon currents are smoothly approximable, or define $[E]\wedge T$ for a singular test merely by its smooth class pairing. A global threshold need not equal a threshold restricted to one type. The positive-residual calculation characterizes the specified divisorial class, and proves strict loss for smooth positive data; it supplies no converse from an annihilating face at a general $L^1$ global threshold and no characterization for arbitrary prescribed types.

supplemental_entries.title: Completeness under nefness and geometric smoothing compatibility
supplemental_entries.statement: For a divisorial exponential equation in a nef big class, or for data satisfying the geometric smoothing compatibility conditions of \cite[Section 3.1]{DNGL26}, determine whether its positive metric on the regular locus is complete. In the smoothing problem, retain the prescribed nonintegrable divisor pole with coefficient smooth and strictly positive across the divisor.
supplemental_entries.state: Both original completeness assertions have negative answers. Book, Theorem~28.14.2, printed p.~1393 gives a semipositive nef and big background on the blowup of $\mathbb P^2$, with a unique full-mass finite-energy solution, zero Lelong numbers and the prescribed nonintegrable pole with smooth strictly positive coefficient. Its cusp is complete, but a disjoint null exceptional curve is at finite distance. Book, Theorem~28.14.3, printed p.~1399 gives an incomplete auxiliary solution for exact geometric smoothing data on the blowup of $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$. The initial residual is K\"ahler, the original volume is fixed as $\omega^2$, and the resolution, discrepancy and residual-volume identities hold exactly. Its auxiliary class is non-nef. The minimal reference has a divisorial logarithm; the solution adds a zero-Lelong cusp and has finite relative energy. Every dense Zariski open positive regular locus is incomplete in both examples. The earlier non-nef example has an ordinary minimal solution; H\"older residuals and logarithmically weakened torus poles supply further normal-length tests.
supplemental_entries.gap: The original question is settled for its two separate regimes. Further refinements are completeness under simultaneous nefness and exact smoothing compatibility, and completeness for an actual evolving maximal flow. The compatible elliptic example has a non-nef class; the nef example chooses its smooth volume as part of the construction. Neither identifies its auxiliary solution with an evolving flow metric. The conditional big-endpoint local convergence theorem discussed in P12 also does not establish completeness.
supplemental_entries.status: resolved in original two separate regimes; joint and evolving-flow refinements open

supplemental_entries.title: Higher-dimensional growing-jet limits and transfer through fibrations
supplemental_entries.statement: Formulate and prove higher-dimensional analogues of the growing-jet transition in P22, and criteria transferring such local limits through Hermitian fibrations. Specify the vanishing ideal, local curvature degeneracy, moving observation scale, Hilbert norm, and intrinsic section-growth normalization.
supplemental_entries.state:
A precise compact sufficient-condition class is proved in Section~27.15, printed p.~1323. Let $Y=(\mathbb P^1)^q$, $q\geq2$, $L=\boxtimes_j\mathcal O(r_j+1)$, with unequal integers $r_j\geq2$ and $\varepsilon_j>0$. In the affine frame use $\phi=\sum_j\log(1+|z_j|^{2r_j}+\varepsilon_j|z_j|^{2r_j+2})$ and the smooth volume $\nu_Y=\prod_j(1+|z_j|^2)^{-2}\mathrm dA_j$, of total mass $\pi^q$. For ordinary point jets $V_m=H^0(Y,L^m\otimes\mathfrak m_x^{k_m})$, $k_m\to\infty$, $k_m=o(m)$, put $t_j=|z_j|^2$, $\psi_j(t)=\log(1+t^{r_j}+\varepsilon_jt^{r_j+1})$, $H_j=t\psi_j'$, $G_j=tH_j'$ and $g_j=G_j/t$. If $mH_j(t_j)/k_m\to\alpha_j>0$, $\sum_j\alpha_j=1$, and $(\sum_jmH_j(t_j)-k_m)/\sqrt{\sum_jmG_j(t_j)}\to\tau$, then
\[
 \frac{\pi^q a(t)B_m(z)}{m^q\prod_jg_j(t_j)}\longrightarrow\Phi(\tau),
 \qquad a(t)=\prod_j(1+t_j)^{-2}.
\]
This includes every sublinear order with the actual radial center. Exact global monomials give $\dim V_m=\prod_j((r_j+1)m+1)-\binom{k_m+q-1}{q}$ and $m^{-q}B_m\nu_Y\to c_1(L,h)^q/q!$ in total variation (Book, Theorem~27.15.1, printed p.~1325). The homogeneous center has the sharp smaller range $k_m=o(m^{2/(r_*+2)})$, $r_*:=\max_jr_j$; positive first remainders produce a nonzero critical Gaussian shift and supercritical limit one (Book, Proposition~27.15.1, printed p.~1327).

For a compact holomorphic submersion $\pi:X\to Y$ with connected fibers of dimension $f\geq1$, a pullback bundle and metric and a matched smooth volume $\pi_*\nu_X=\nu_Y$, the moving isolated selector $\varphi_m=(k_m+q+f-1)\chi_p/m$ has $\mathcal I(m\varphi_m)=\mathfrak m_p^{k_m}$. Its pole and ideal do not descend, but selected sections and their smooth norms identify exactly with $V_m$. Thus $B_{X,m}=B_m\circ\pi$, the growth exponent is $q$, and the lifted density converges in total variation. Matched volumes exist on every such submersion; arbitrary volumes instead transform the base norm, for which this local theorem has not been proved (Book, Theorem~27.15.2, printed p.~1329). This moving selector does not close the fixed-selector problem P21.

At a fixed zero of curvature, an explicit smooth semipositive metric on $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^2}(1)$ already gives the unselected kernel scale $B_m(p)=3m/(\pi^2\rho_0\log m)(1+O((\log m)^{-1}))$ for a smooth positive two-torus-invariant probability volume with local density $\rho_0$ (Book, Proposition~27.14.1, printed p.~1322). The leading constant is $3/2$ for Fubini--Study probability volume. The metric is the exact model of \cite[Example I.15, pp.~9--10]{ChiangKernel26}; the manuscript proves the norm asymptotic directly by elementary integrals. No growing vanishing ideal or moving-scale limit is included in this example.
supplemental_entries.gap: Extend beyond the specified separable radial class: mixed or angular remainders, observation faces with some zero energy fractions, other compact bases or ideals, and general fiber-selected singularities. Control global section production and the transformed norm at the moving scale in each new regime. The proved sufficient conditions do not imply a universal Gaussian expression or an ambient-dimensional Monge--Amp\`ere limit.

supplemental_entries.title: Individual solvability criteria for arbitrary non-pluripolar measures
supplemental_entries.source: Book, Lemma~1.6.7, printed p.~26; Proposition~14.25.1, printed p.~642; Corollary~14.25.1, printed p.~643; Theorem~14.25.1, printed p.~643; Theorem~14.24.1, printed p.~640; Theorem~14.4.2, printed p.~542; Proposition~1.8.1, printed p.~49; Lemma~1.21.5, printed p.~109; Lemma~1.21.6, printed p.~109; Proposition~10.3.1, printed p.~370; Proposition~14.30.1, printed p.~666; Theorem~14.30.2, printed p.~667.
supplemental_entries.statement: Extend the individual-density threshold criterion from $f\,\mathrm dV$ to a fixed finite nonzero non-pluripolar Borel measure $\nu$. Find an intrinsic criterion for a positive scaled subsolution, an exact normalized equation, and an exponential equation, distinguishing these three assertions.
supplemental_entries.state:
Positive lower mass characterizes solvability for every finite non-pluripolar measure. Prescribed-reference versions have their explicit model and lower-volume assumptions. At zero lower mass some absolutely continuous probability measures already admit no positive scaled subsolution, while smooth densities remain solvable. For individual densities, bounded truncations and the Gauduchon root formula give an exact subsolution criterion. Proposition~14.30.1, printed p.~666 gives an exact finite-mass equation on $X_0	imes\mathbb P^1$ for $
u=M(h_0^m/V_0)\otimes\mu$, where $\mu$ is any non-polar probability and $\kappa$ is mass-one Fubini--Study. Its coefficient is $(m+1)V_0/M$; the separated solution is unique up to constants, bounded exactly when its logarithmic potential $Q_\mu$ is bounded, and continuous exactly when $Q_\mu$ is continuous. Lemma~14.30.2, printed p.~662 proves the canonical Sobolev measure trace when $Q_\mu$ is finite and continuous. Theorem~14.30.1, printed p.~664 then gives a unique bounded continuous curve equation for every positive exponent, with fixed barriers and whole-family uniform selection at rate $O(\lambda)$. Theorem~14.30.2, printed p.~667 identifies and attains the product coefficient over all genuine scaled subsolutions, including competitors with additional poles or infinite mass. Its bounded exponential solution is greatest over all genuine exponential subsolutions, and unique among bounded solutions. The supremum-normalized equation retains its scalar $c_\lambda=c\exp(\lambda\sup w_\lambda)$. Proposition~14.30.2, printed p.~668 supplies a Frostman ball test, including nonconstant weighted circle measures singular with respect to smooth volume. If $v_-(h_0)=0$, the product is nonclosed and has zero lower mass; this remains a factor hypothesis. Proposition~14.25.1, printed p.~642 constructs a fixed singular non-pluripolar probability $ho=S_n^{-1}\sum_j r_j^{n/2}\sigma_j$ on shrinking coordinate spheres, with $r_j=r_0 2^{-j}$, and a strict $1/2$-H"older reference satisfying $\mathrm{MA}_h(u_ho)\geq kho$ on every Hermitian background. For a finite nonzero $
u$ with $\|\mathrm d
u/\mathrm dho\|_{L^\infty(ho)}<\infty$, Theorem~14.25.1, printed p.~643 gives a positive scaled subsolution and, for each positive exponent, a unique bounded exact exponential solution of positive finite mass. The fixed scalar has no supremum-zero normalization. This includes bounded densities on one sphere, without a product decomposition, positive lower mass or bounded upper mass. Proposition~10.3.1, printed p.~370 gives a separate one-sided stability estimate for solution measures bounded by the square of capacity, with exponent $1/(6n+1)$. Theorem~14.24.1, printed p.~640 proves the sufficient range condition $
u\leq A\mathrm{MA}_h(u)$ for a H"older reference: there are $c>0$ and a normalized H"older potential $w$ with $\mathrm{MA}_h(w)=c
u$ and positive finite mass. Corollary~14.25.1, printed p.~643 applies it to the fixed spherical test, using $A=M_ho(
u)/k$. The proof includes continuous-density approximation, a smooth-reference diagonal, two-sided coefficient bounds and uniform convergence. Theorem~14.4.2, printed p.~542 gives exponent $\alpha/[(\alpha+2n)(6n+1)+\alpha]$ for an already continuous solution dominated by a $C^{0,\alpha}$ reference. Its local integral, capacity, approximation and weighted-smoothing dependencies are proved in Chapter~1.
supplemental_entries.gap: For a general $\nu$, there is no canonical bounded-density truncation relative to smooth volume. Replace this construction while retaining measure domination and finite-mass compactness. This extends P07/S03 and is not implied by solving all smooth densities. The logarithmic-potential criterion supplies all three assertions in the specified product regime, without smooth-density truncation. supplemental_entries.title: Automatic envelope genuineness in semipositive dual attainment
supplemental_entries.statement: Suppose a positive-threshold $L^1$ density has a smooth semipositive maximizing Gauduchon current, strictly positive off a proper analytic set $Z$, and let $\Phi_f$ be the greatest normalized threshold subsolution. Find conditions making $P_{\delta h}(\Phi_f)$ genuine for some $0<\delta<1$, and determine regularity across $Z$. More generally, ask whether moment or entropy control forces this envelope condition.
supplemental_entries.state: The semipositive maximizer gives a unique exact global threshold solution, smoothness off $Z$, a fixed lower barrier and whole-family normalized $L^1$ convergence of exponential solutions. A genuine smaller-background envelope upgrades to capacity convergence; $L^p$ data, $p>1$, give continuity and uniform convergence. For rough maximizing currents, first moments plus this envelope condition yield an exact cluster equation. Entropy bounds supply moments and uniform integrability but do not supply the envelope. Book, Theorem~26.9.3, printed p.~1098 now proves genuine obstacle envelopes at every smaller scale and zero Lelong numbers for all full-mass potentials when $\ddc(h^j)=0$ for $1\leq j<n$, and gives the exact density threshold $V/\int_Xf\,\mathrm{d}V$. Book, Proposition~26.9.6, printed p.~1099 gives explicit all-scale competitors from a quantitative sublinear singularity bound. Book, Theorem~26.9.4, printed p.~1100 proves smooth extension across $Z$ under attainment, zero Lelong numbers and a globally smooth semipositive root of complex rank at least two everywhere. Book, Example~26.9.2, printed p.~1101 and Book, Example~26.9.3, printed p.~1101 verify actual attained Hopf and ramified quadric instances. These are restricted sufficient conditions; a smooth maximizing current alone does not supply a smooth root with the required rank. Book, Proposition~26.9.7, printed p.~1103 computes an explicit unbounded full-mass point-pole threshold solution with genuine smaller-background envelopes at every scale, an $L^1$ density in no $L^p$ for $p>1$, and no smooth semipositive maximizing test. Book, Corollary~26.9.6, printed p.~1104 gives its exact finite-entropy and weighted-integrability parameter ranges. These are properties of the single equation density; the example does not satisfy the smooth semipositive attainment hypothesis and does not settle the original uniform probability question.
supplemental_entries.gap: Determine whether general moment or entropy control forces a genuine smaller-background envelope in the attained setting, or identify its failure there. Invariant bounded mass and a quantified sublinear lower singularity bound now give sufficient conditions. The across-set theorem also requires a globally smooth root of rank at least two and zero Lelong numbers; remove or replace those hypotheses only with an additional proof. Capacity convergence under a genuine envelope and exact solvability in the semipositive attained regime remain distinct from these intrinsic-condition questions.

supplemental_entries.state: Finite divisor residuals have explicit mass polynomials and Gauduchon variation formulas. Closed class-$\mathcal C$ restricted invariants are resolution independent; closed K\"ahler positive products and volume differentiability are literature inputs. For nonclosed nef backgrounds, irrational or oscillatory volume orders and modification jumps obstruct direct transfer of the closed numerical formulas. The nonclosed ruled family with an imposed nonanalytic ordinary type is now explicit: for $\theta=cw_1+aw_2$ and the type $bG_p+1-(1-G_p)^\alpha$ on $Y=\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$, where $w$ is the probability Fubini--Study form, $\ddc G_p=[p]-w$, $c>0$, $b\geq0$, $a>0$ is smooth on the first sphere and $0<\alpha<1$, all rough competitors have finite positive mass when $b<c$, with lower and upper volumes $2(c-b)\min a$ and $2(c-b)\max a$ (Theorem~19.10.1, printed p.~950). This includes the infinite closed-first-moment range $\alpha\geq1/2$. Smooth gauges and pure pullback preserve both masses (Proposition~19.10.2, printed p.~953). For smooth first-factor $m>0$ with $\int mw=1$, the separate fixed-density all-test Gauduchon volume is $2(c-b)/\int(m/a)w$, with an attained infimum and exact moving cost (Proposition~26.21.3, printed p.~1225; Corollary~26.21.1, printed p.~1226). The smooth nef endpoint has zero variational volume and is not big, while the upper ordinary-type volume tends to $4$.

A solution needs a precise construction accounting for differential background data and the distinction between upper singularity volume and fixed-density variational volume. These restricted data do not define a general moving positive product, and the nonbig zero-volume endpoint does not decide a positive-volume bigness bridge.

supplemental_entries.title: Optimal multiweight ideal distance when the number of weights exceeds the dimension
supplemental_entries.statement:
Fix integers $n\geq2$, $r>n$, and real exponents $p_1,\ldots,p_r>1$. Determine the smallest universal constant $C(n;p_1,\ldots,p_r)$ such that the following inequality holds on every pseudoconvex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb C^n$: for genuine psh $\psi$, genuine negative psh $\phi_i$, and holomorphic $f$ with $0<I=\int_\Omega|f|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi-\sum_i\phi_i}\,\mathrm dV<+\infty$,
\[
 \inf\left\{\int_\Omega|g|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi}\,\mathrm dV:
       g\in\mathcal O(\Omega),\quad
       f-g\in\sum_{i=1}^r\Gamma(\Omega,\mathcal I(p_i\phi_i+\psi))\right\}
       \leq C(n;p_1,\ldots,p_r)I.
\]
Global ideal membership means local integrability at every germ; it does not require a finite global norm for the subtracted sections. Establish both the universal upper estimate and examples attaining it or approaching it.
supplemental_entries.state:
Book Theorem~1.16.2, printed p.~76, proves the upper constant $\prod_i(1-1/p_i)$ for every $r$, with equality models when $r\leq n$. Theorem~1.16.3, printed pp.~78--82, determines the optimal constant $\max\{1-\sum_i1/p_i,0\}$ for every $r$ in dimension one; when the reciprocal sum is at least one, $g=0$ is admissible. Takakura's exact preprint \cite[v1, Theorem~1.2 and Example~3.2, pp.~1--2 and 7]{TakDivision26} states the dimension-dependent bound $1-\frac{\sum_i1/p_i}{\min\{n,r\}}$ under $\sum_i1/p_i<\min\{n,r\}$ and asks about optimality. Its general higher-rank proof is not an adopted input of the manuscript; the book reconstructs scalar division and the stated product and planar estimates directly.
Book Example~1.16.2, printed pp.~79--83, constructs unit-ball hyperplane weights with equal exponents $p$, for every $n\geq2$, $r>n$ and $r/n<p\leq r$. The reciprocal sum is in $[1,n)$, the input integral is finite, and the distance equals $\pi^n/n!>0$. It gives a positive lower bound $\pi^n/(n!I)$ for the corresponding universal constant and excludes extending the planar zero regime to higher dimensions. It does not determine the optimal constant.
supplemental_entries.gap: For $n\geq2$ and $r>n$, the known product estimate has no equality argument using $r$ distinct coordinate directions. Determine how the common zero sets and the interaction of multiplier ideals affect the optimal constant. The planar principal-ideal calculation does not extend to arbitrary higher-dimensional ideals. This is a local quantitative problem, distinct from global $\mathcal I$-goodness in P01/P06.
